## Current State

The pipeline driver's implementer worker runs headless with a narrow Bash allow list (`plugin/bin/lib/driver/roles.js`): the declared test command (`Bash(node tools/run-tests.js --files-from *)` on this repo) plus read-only `git status/diff/log/show/ls-files`, with `autoAllowBashIfSandboxed: false`, so any other command, including a compound one that chains the allowed command, is denied.

The worker prompt (`plugin/bin/lib/driver/steps.js`, the `Tests:` line in the implementer prompt builder) says only: "write their repo-relative paths, one per line, to `.claude-tweaks/pipelines/worker-test-files.txt` and run `{testCommand}` with {files} as that path." It never says (a) Bash admits only that command and read-only git, (b) the list file is written with the Write tool, or (c) the test command must run alone, unchained.

Observed live on 2026-11-23 in the #5571 proof drain (`drive.js 5270 --run .claude-tweaks/pipelines/2026-11-23T151537-record-5270 --no-settle`, plugin 6.176.0): the worker edited three files, then issued two Bash calls that were denied: a `python3 - <<'E' …` heredoc edit, and `mkdir -p .claude-tweaks/pipelines && printf '…' > .claude-tweaks/pipelines/worker-test-files.txt && node tools/run-tests.js --files-from .claude-tweaks/pipelines/worker-test-files.txt 2>&1 | tail -40`. It then reported `cannot-complete` ("The Bash tool was denied in this session, so the edits are unverified and nothing is committed"), never running the allowed command on its own. The driver's final line: `outcome: express-escalated`, `stop.reason: express-error`, `denialCount: 2`, `costUsd: 0.206`, 18 turns. The record fell back to the full `/flow` path, so the driver lane delivered nothing for an admitted record.

This blocks #5571 AC2 (an admitted record must reach `merged`/`armed`/`pending-review` through the driver) and so Phase 13 (#6117-#6120).

## Deliverables

- [ ] The implementer prompt's `Tests:` line (`plugin/bin/lib/driver/steps.js`) tells the worker: write the test list with the Write tool; run the declared test command as one Bash call on its own (no `&&`, `;`, pipe, redirect or `mkdir`); Bash otherwise admits only read-only `git status/diff/log/show/ls-files`; make edits with Edit/Write, never a shell script.
- [ ] The prompt tells the worker a denied Bash call means that command shape is outside the allow list, not that Bash is unavailable: retry with the allowed form before reporting `cannot-complete`.
- [ ] Unit tests in `tests/bin-lib/driver/worker.test.js` (or wherever the implementer prompt is asserted today) pin both sentences, rendered with a declared test command.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The implementer prompt rendered with a declared test command contains an instruction to write the test list with the Write tool and to run the test command alone, unchained, and names read-only git as the only other Bash it may run.
2. The rendered prompt contains an instruction that a denied Bash call is a disallowed command shape, to be retried in the allowed form, not a reason to stop.
3. With no declared test command (the "do not run tests" branch), the prompt is unchanged apart from any shared edit-with-Edit/Write sentence.
4. A test fails when either instruction is removed from the prompt builder (verified by reverting the prompt change).
5. `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

Driver-built records no longer fall back to the slow path because the worker misread a refused test command as Bash being switched off.

## Technical Approach

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/driver/steps.js` — implementer prompt `Tests:` line — Write-tool list file, unchained test command, denial-is-shape guidance
- `tests/bin-lib/driver/worker.test.js` — pin the new prompt sentences

Surface: backend
Risk-flags: none

## Overview

Make the driver mirror its step status into station events with the new outcome vocabulary, an actor and a reason code. This is task 5 of 8 in the plan "Factory Floor Map: claude-tweaks Emission Implementation Plan". Goal of the whole plan: claude-tweaks code writes, for the `build a record` process, the plan when a record is claimed, an outcome with reason and actor at every transition it performs, and hold and release facts, as new lines in the station-event file. The extension point is the existing emitter in `plugin/bin/lib/station-events/`, whose single vocabulary home is `stations.js`. New facts are new event kinds and new `payload` fields on existing kinds, so the file stays version 1 and old readers ignore what they do not know.

**Complexity:** Medium
**Estimated tasks:** 5

## Non-Goals

- Hub-side reading, folding or display of these events (the hub plan, `thn-inc/dispatch`).
- Any other task of this plan: each of the eight records owns exactly its own Files.
- Cutting a release; claude-tweaks ships by release tag and that is the owner's decision.
- No prose is asked to log: no skill text is changed to emit events.

## Prerequisites

| Record | Title | Status |
|---|---|---|
| E1 | Floor map, emission 1/8: Capture pass: transition code by station, and the station order from real moves | must be merged before this starts (native blocked-by edge) |
| E2 | Floor map, emission 2/8: Vocabulary and validation | must be merged before this starts (native blocked-by edge) |

## Current State

Spec: `/Users/thomasholknielsen/Code Workspaces/factory/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-23-factory-floor-map-design.md` (also landing in `thn-inc/dispatch` at `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-23-factory-floor-map-design.md`; the plans at `docs/superpowers/plans/`). Sections that apply: "The model", "Outcomes and reasons", "Events", and Order step 0.

Repository: `/Users/thomasholknielsen/Code Workspaces/claude-tweaks` (`thn-inc/claude-tweaks`). Test runner: `node tools/run-tests.js <file.test.js>`; stack Node.js (CommonJS) with `node:test`.

#### The event contract (shared with the hub plan)

Lines keep their existing fields (`v: 1`, `eventKey`, `repoName`, `recordNumber`, `kind`, `station`, `at`, `outcome`, `lane`, `sessionId`, `runId`, `payload`). New:

| Kind | Filed under station | `payload` |
|---|---|---|
| `planned` | the station the item is at when written (at the claim: `build`) | `{ process: 'build-a-record', processVersion: 1, list: string, stations: string[], reasonCode: string, reasonText?: string }`; `stations` is the full ordered list, including stations already passed |
| `replanned` | the station the item is at | `{ stations: string[], reasonCode: string, reasonText?: string, cause: { kind: 'outcome' \| 'decision' \| 'config', ref?: string } }` |
| `held` | the station the item is at | `{ why: 'blocked' \| 'parked' \| 'changes-requested' \| 'waiting-on-you', ref?: string }` |
| `released` | the station the item is at | `{ why: <same set> }` |
| `decided` | the station the decision was made at | `{ decision: 'authorize' \| 'accept' \| 'unblock', actor: string, via: 'panel' \| 'skill' \| 'rule', outcomeRef: string }` (`outcomeRef` is the `eventKey` of the `exited` it caused) |
| `exited` (extended) | unchanged | `outcome` is one of `passed \| sent-back \| failed \| stopped`; `payload.actor` always; `payload.reasonCode` for every outcome except `passed`; `payload.next` (a station id) for `sent-back`; `payload.reasonText?` |

`actor` is `agent`, `script`, `person` or `rule:<id>`. Reason codes are the closed list `REASON_CODES` (Task 2). A reason nothing knows is `unspecified`.

### Global Constraints that apply to this task

- "No prose is asked to log; only code that already makes the transition does." Every new line is written from code that already performs the transition.
- "A reason that nothing knows is `unspecified`, counted and shown, never silently dropped, and never blocks the outcome."
- "Four outcomes: `passed`, `sent-back`, `failed`, `stopped`. Held is a state, not an outcome. A skip is a `replanned` event."
- Every station name, kind, outcome and lane literal lives in `plugin/bin/lib/station-events/stations.js`; `tests/bin-lib/station-events/station-literal-conformance.test.js` scans for violations.
- Emission never blocks or fails a transition (`appendStationEvent` already drops a bad line to stderr and returns).

## Deliverables

Files:

- Modify: `plugin/bin/lib/station-events/stations.js` (`DRIVER_STATUS_OUTCOMES`), `plugin/bin/lib/station-events/driver-mirror.js`, `plugin/bin/lib/driver/run.js`
- Test: `tests/bin-lib/station-events/driver-mirror.test.js`, `tests/bin-lib/driver/run.test.js`

Interfaces:

- Produces: `DRIVER_STATUS_OUTCOMES = { ok: 'passed', fail: 'failed', stop: <per Task 1> }`; driver `exited` lines carry `payload.actor: 'script'` for `ci`/`merge`/`pr` steps and `'agent'` for `worker`/`test`/`review`, and `payload.reasonCode: 'test-failed'` for a failed `test` step, `'infrastructure'` for a failed `ci` step whose failure is classified as infrastructure by the driver, otherwise `'unspecified'`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The task's tests exist and pass, exactly as the plan states them: **Step 1: Write failing tests:** `a failed test step mirrors to exited failed with reasonCode test-failed and actor agent`; `a failed ci step classified infrastructure mirrors with reasonCode infrastructure`; `an ok step mirrors to exited passed with actor`; `a step with no known reason mirrors with reasonCode unspecified`.
2. Review focus, covered by the tests above: A transition whose code path cannot name a reason writes `unspecified` and still writes the `exited` line.

## Release Note

Made driver exits write an outcome with actor and reason code into the station-event file.

## Technical Approach

### Data / API Surface

The interfaces under Deliverables are the contract surface for this record; the event contract in Current State is the shared line shape.

### Task steps (from the plan, in order)

- [ ] **Step 1: Write failing tests:** `a failed test step mirrors to exited failed with reasonCode test-failed and actor agent`; `a failed ci step classified infrastructure mirrors with reasonCode infrastructure`; `an ok step mirrors to exited passed with actor`; `a step with no known reason mirrors with reasonCode unspecified`.
- [ ] **Step 2: Run** `node tools/run-tests.js tests/bin-lib/station-events/driver-mirror.test.js tests/bin-lib/driver/run.test.js`. Expected: FAIL.
- [ ] **Step 3: Implement** the mapping in `driver-mirror.js`; use the driver's existing failure classification for `ci`, and write `unspecified` where none exists.
- [ ] **Step 4: Run** the Step 2 command. Expected: PASS.
- [ ] **Step 5: Commit** `feat: driver exits carry outcome, actor and reason`.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/station-events/stations.js`
- `plugin/bin/lib/station-events/driver-mirror.js`
- `plugin/bin/lib/driver/run.js`
- `tests/bin-lib/station-events/driver-mirror.test.js`
- `tests/bin-lib/driver/run.test.js`

## Gotchas

- Changes the driver status-to-outcome mapping.
- Where a step says "the code Task 1 names" or "per Task 1", read the sections of `docs/reference/station-events.md` that record 1/8 (E1) merges; they are the source of those names and lists.
- Emission never blocks or fails a transition: `appendStationEvent` drops a bad line to stderr and returns; do not add a throw on any emission path.


<!-- work-fingerprint: factory-floor-map-emission:emission-5 -->
work-fingerprint: factory-floor-map-emission:emission-5

## Decisions (orchestrator, 2026-11-23)

If this record needs a reason code that is not in `REASON_CODES` (`plugin/bin/lib/station-events/stations.js`), it may add the code to that list with a test and make no other change to that file. Lines this record writes carry `payload.actor`, so they get the full checks of the contract.

## Decisions on the plan review (orchestrator, 2026-11-23, answering its two questions)

1. **Red tests are the `test-failed` case: Reading B.** The driver's test step returns `status: 'stop'` with detail `red tests` for red tests, and `status: 'fail'` only when `verify.js` gives no verdict. Mirror them like this:
   - test step, `stop`, detail `red tests` -> `exited` outcome `failed`, `reasonCode: 'test-failed'`, actor `agent`.
   - test step, `fail`, a verdictless detail (timeout, spawn error, exit 2, the `verdictlessDetail` cases) -> outcome `failed`, `reasonCode: 'infrastructure'`, actor `agent`.
   - test step, `fail` from an interrupted run -> outcome `failed`, `reasonCode: 'unspecified'`.
   - any other driver `stop` (any step, any other reason) -> outcome `stopped`, `reasonCode: 'unspecified'`, `reasonText` set to the driver's reason; the `stop` entry of `DRIVER_STATUS_OUTCOMES` stays `stopped`, and this red-tests case is the one detail-keyed exception to it.
   Revised tests: `a red-tests stop at the test step mirrors to exited failed with reasonCode test-failed and actor agent`; `a verdictless fail at the test step mirrors to exited failed with reasonCode infrastructure`; `an interrupted fail at the test step mirrors to exited failed with reasonCode unspecified`; `a stop at any other step mirrors to exited stopped with reasonCode unspecified and the driver reason in reasonText`. The Acceptance Criterion that says "a failed test step" means the red-tests case above.
2. **`ci` infrastructure classification: Reading A.** A `ci` line whose detail is `read-failed`, `gh-absent` or `no-pr` and whose exit is non-passing gets `infrastructure`; the `ci` step always reports `ok` today, so this branch is exercised only by a test line, and every real `ci` line is written as the driver gives it (`passed`, actor `script`). State the gap in the pull request description and in `docs/reference/station-events.md` under the driver mapping: "a red CI state is data for the reviewer, not an exit; it is not mirrored as a failure."

## Current State

Under `consoleAutoResolve`, `console-resolve.js --policy console-auto` computes the merge half once and persists it to `{run-dir}/console.json` as `merge.resolution`. `mergeResolution()` in `plugin/bin/lib/console/resolve.js` honours a needs-human verdict only through `needsHumanVerdict(decisions)`, which reads `decisions.md` at that moment.

`wrap-up/execution-and-verification.md`'s Branch finish then routes the pr-first merge on `console.json`'s `merge.resolution` directly, and `_shared/pr-first-merge.md` never re-reads a needs-human verdict. `review-console.md` orders the Auto-merge short-circuit (which logs the `assess-agent-autonomy` merge-check verdict) before the Auto-resolution short-circuit, but nothing mechanical enforces that order.

Observed in run `2026-11-16T183913-record-5770` (#5770, PR #5780): `console-resolve.js` ran at 20:12:39Z and recorded `merge.resolution: merge`; the short-circuit's `needs-human` verdict was logged at 20:13:22Z, 43 seconds later. Only the dispatched agent's manual hold kept the PR from merging.

## Deliverables

1. At Branch finish, before acting on `merge.resolution: merge`, re-evaluate `needsHumanVerdict` against the current `decisions.md`. On a hit, resolve leave-open (`pending-review`) and log one decision line naming the late verdict.
2. Have `console-resolve.js` refuse to resolve the merge half, or mark it stale, when the Auto-merge short-circuit applies to the run (live `auto:build` + `auto:merge`/`auto:merge-pending`) but no merge-check verdict line exists yet.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A test where `decisions.md` gains a needs-human merge-check line after `console.json` records `merge.resolution: merge` shows Branch finish leaving the PR open, never merging.
- A test where `console-resolve.js` runs with the short-circuit applicable and no verdict line yet shows it not resolving `merge`.
- The in-order path (verdict logged before the resolve) is unchanged: existing `console-resolve` tests stay green.

## Release Note

An unattended run no longer merges a PR whose merge check asked for a human, even when the check finished after the Review Console resolved.

## Technical Approach

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/console/resolve.js` — needsHumanVerdict / mergeResolution: refuse or mark stale before a verdict exists
- `plugin/bin/console-resolve.js` — surface the stale merge half
- `plugin/skills/wrap-up/execution-and-verification.md` — Branch finish re-checks the verdict before merging
- `plugin/skills/wrap-up/review-console.md` — state the ordering requirement as enforced

**Related:** #5383 (its wrap-up staged all three changes below; they are coupled, so they are filed together)

Origin: wrap-up of #5383 (staged/skills-1.patch, staged/skills-2.md, staged/reflect-1.md)

Defer-reason: genuinely-larger

## Current State

Both files of `.claude/skills/gh-api-module-pattern/` are over the 52,500-byte Read rail (`plugin/bin/lib/skill-audit/budgets.js` `RAIL_BYTES`), measured with `context-cost.js`'s `measuredBytes` at 33f635d03: `cli-wrapper-contract.md` 56,381 (over by 3,881), `SKILL.md` 53,799 (over by 1,299). Both were over before #5383, which grew them by 26 and 355 bytes. The `rail:` tests cover only the plugin's shipped skills, so CI never flags these.

#5383's wrap-up found two additions `cli-wrapper-contract.md` needs, both of which grow it further:
1. The relative-path and live-stdio rules. #5383's review fix wave (46a856cf1) resolved relative path arguments against `deps.cwd()` four different ways across five CLIs, and an unconditional `path.resolve(deps.cwd(), p)` broke a test because it read cwd for absolute paths too. release-local's hook needs inherited stdio for real callers, or an npm OTP prompt fails. The contract states neither rule.
2. The env-only fixture proof in the conversion-proofs bullet sets `GIT_DIR` alone. That leaves `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` at the cwd repo (probed: `GIT_DIR` only prints A; `GIT_DIR` plus `GIT_WORK_TREE=<B>` prints B). The bullet also has no rule for observing the injected `cwd`: a stub that records `process.cwd()` per call, as #5383's digest-rollover AC6.1 fix does.

The diff staged for addition 2, from a real `git diff` (it applied cleanly at 33f635d03):

```diff
diff --git a/.claude/skills/gh-api-module-pattern/cli-wrapper-contract.md b/.claude/skills/gh-api-module-pattern/cli-wrapper-contract.md
index e63de77d3..ffedfa987 100644
--- a/.claude/skills/gh-api-module-pattern/cli-wrapper-contract.md
+++ b/.claude/skills/gh-api-module-pattern/cli-wrapper-contract.md
@@ -2,7 +2,7 @@
 
 - Logic lives in an exported `run(argv, deps)`; every side effect (`runner`, `ghAvailable`, `remoteUrl`, `stdout`, `stderr`) goes through `deps` so tests inject fakes. **Every** `deps` call that can throw (e.g. `remoteUrl` outside a git repo) is try/caught into the documented exit-code contract — an un-wrapped deps call is where #610's one post-review high landed.
 - **A CLI that tests call in-process meets the entry contract** (#5374; `plugin/bin/resolve-policy.js` is the worked example). It exports `run` and `realDeps`; `argv` is `process.argv.slice(2)`, and `run` returns an integer exit code or a Promise of one. The script entry is the file's last statement: `if (require.main === module) process.exitCode = run(process.argv.slice(2), realDeps);`. The standard io keys, each present only when the CLI uses it, are `stdout(text)`, `stderr(text)`, `cwd()`, `env` (a plain object, read-only), `stdin()` (the whole input as a string) and `homeDir()`. Above the guard and in everything `run` calls there is no `process.exitCode`, `process.exit()`, `process.chdir()` or write to `process.env`. A relative path is resolved against `deps.cwd()`, never left to `path.resolve` or `fs`. Every child process is started with a `cwd` derived from `deps.cwd()` and with `env: deps.env`, and a library function on the CLI's path takes that `env` as an option whose default is the inherited environment, so a `gh` or `git` stub on an injected `PATH` is not skipped. The process-wide timeout knobs are the named exception: `plugin/bin/lib/shared-primitives.js`'s shared `gh`/`git` timeouts read `CLAUDE_TWEAKS_GH_TIMEOUT_MS`, `CLAUDE_TWEAKS_GIT_TIMEOUT_MS` and the `gh-timeout-ms` / `git-timeout-ms` keys of the `policy.yml` at the real working directory once per process, and `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/git-exec.js`'s `runGit` reads `CT_HOOKS_GIT_TIMEOUT_MS` from the real `process.env`, by design; an in-process test cannot set them through `env`, so a test of those knobs is a `spawnCli` test. Tests call the CLI through `tests/helpers/run-cli.js` (`runCli`, or `runCliSync` for a synchronous `run`), passing an absolute `cliPath`; the helper fails the test on a leaked `process.exitCode`, working directory, `process.env` key, signal listener, direct stdout/stderr write, or an `os.homedir()` call under an injected home; each converted CLI keeps one or two `spawnCli` smoke tests for the script entry, shebang and exit code. The helper's `env` defaults to `{}` and is the whole environment the CLI sees, so a CLI that starts `git` or `gh` needs `PATH` (and `SystemRoot` on Windows) in the `env` the test passes. Module-level state under `plugin/bin` (the forge probe's memos, for example) survives between in-process calls in one test file; a case that depends on it passes `fresh: true`, which clears `require.cache` under `plugin/bin` first. The helper fails closed: after merging `realDeps` with the test's fakes, it replaces a key named in `FAIL_CLOSED_KEYS` (`runner`, `gh`, `ghAvailable`, `runHook`, `spawn`) that still holds the CLI's real value with a function that throws, and records the reach so a CLI that catches the throw still fails the test; `allowRealRunner: true` lifts it for one call. The list is by key name: a `realDeps` key that can start `gh` or an arbitrary command carries one of those names, and a record converting a CLI whose `realDeps` holds such a seam under another name (for example `execFileSync`, `runPremiseCheck`) adds that name to `FAIL_CLOSED_KEYS` in the same change. A git-only seam (`git`, `gitRunner`) is deliberately not on the list: it runs real git against the injected `cwd` and `env`, which is the behaviour under test. `tests/bin-lib/cli-entry-conformance.test.js` pins the three structural rules (exports `run`, has the guard, no `process.exitCode`/`process.exit(` above it) for every top-level `plugin/bin/*.js`, with a `NOT_YET` list that only shrinks; `hooks.js` is the standing exception (its entry calls `process.exit(code)` and it has a require-time prefilter).
-- **Converting an existing CLI to the entry contract takes two proofs the tests-side journey does not cover.** `docs/journeys/call-a-plugin-bin-cli-in-process-from-a-test-5374.md` starts from a CLI that already meets the contract; the `plugin/bin` side of the change needs these first. (1) Pin the script's output with real-process tests committed before the split, so the split is checked against the old behavior and not against itself: #5374 committed five `resolve-policy.js` script cases in `tests/resolve-policy-entry.test.js` (8fa20f94e) before splitting the file into a core and a printing `run` (75fb7d40e). (2) Prove that each `git` or `gh` child on the CLI's path got the injected `env` with an env-only fixture, not by reading the call: two repos, A with no remote and B with an `origin` and a recorded `origin/HEAD`, the CLI's `cwd` in A and `GIT_DIR=<B>/.git` only in the injected `env`, so a child that inherits the real environment reads A and a child that got `env: deps.env` reads B's remote (`forgePair` in `tests/forge-probe-env.test.js` and `tests/resolve-policy-entry.test.js`). Strip `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, `GIT_INDEX_FILE` and `GIT_COMMON_DIR` from the fixture's own setup `git` calls, so a variable the test runner inherited cannot point them at the wrong repo. Find the ambient reads on a CLI's path by running each documented invocation through `runCliSync` and through `spawnCli` against the same fixture, with an injected `cwd`, `env` and `HOME` that differ from the real ones, and comparing the two results, not by reading the code: the read audit for `resolve-policy.js` (#5374) missed sites in four successive passes (plan, plan review, whole-branch review, review phase).
+- **Converting an existing CLI to the entry contract takes two proofs the tests-side journey does not cover.** `docs/journeys/call-a-plugin-bin-cli-in-process-from-a-test-5374.md` starts from a CLI that already meets the contract; the `plugin/bin` side of the change needs these first. (1) Pin the script's output with real-process tests committed before the split, so the split is checked against the old behavior and not against itself: #5374 committed five `resolve-policy.js` script cases in `tests/resolve-policy-entry.test.js` (8fa20f94e) before splitting the file into a core and a printing `run` (75fb7d40e). (2) Prove that each `git` or `gh` child on the CLI's path got the injected `env` with an env-only fixture, not by reading the call: two repos, A with no remote and B with an `origin` and a recorded `origin/HEAD`, the CLI's `cwd` in A and `GIT_DIR=<B>/.git` only in the injected `env`, so a child that inherits the real environment reads A and a child that got `env: deps.env` reads B's remote (`forgePair` in `tests/forge-probe-env.test.js` and `tests/resolve-policy-entry.test.js`). A child that finds the repository root with `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` is not moved by `GIT_DIR` alone: git then takes the working directory as the work tree and still prints A, so put `GIT_WORK_TREE=<B>` beside it in the injected `env`; a child that reads only the repository (`--absolute-git-dir`, `log`, `remote get-url`) follows `GIT_DIR` alone (AC6.1 in `tests/risk-flags-cli.test.js`, #5383). The `cwd` half needs its own observation: a test named for an injected `cwd` whose stub never reads it stays green with the child's `cwd` option deleted, so have the stub append `process.cwd()` to a file on each call and assert every entry equals the injected directory, both sides through `path.resolve(fs.realpathSync(…))` (`gh-cwd.txt` in `tests/digest-rollover-cli.test.js`'s AC6.1 data-call test, #5383). Strip `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, `GIT_INDEX_FILE` and `GIT_COMMON_DIR` from the fixture's own setup `git` calls, so a variable the test runner inherited cannot point them at the wrong repo. Find the ambient reads on a CLI's path by running each documented invocation through `runCliSync` and through `spawnCli` against the same fixture, with an injected `cwd`, `env` and `HOME` that differ from the real ones, and comparing the two results, not by reading the code: the read audit for `resolve-policy.js` (#5374) missed sites in four successive passes (plan, plan review, whole-branch review, review phase).
 - **A fail-closed branch around an injected dependency needs one test of the real dependency's failure shape, not only a stub that throws.** A stub proves the wrapper catches a throw, not that the real dependency ever throws. `plugin/bin/dispatch-resume.js`'s run-dir listing is the example: `read('run dir listing', …)` mapped a throw to exit 4, but the real `listRunDirsWithState` swallows a `readdirSync` failure into an empty listing, so the branch was unreachable and an unlistable pipelines dir passed the bound-run scan as clean (verdict and `--bound-run` modes) and could report this session's own lock as a live sibling. #4809 added `listRunDirsFailClosed` and the tests that drive the real dependency.
 - `require.main === module` guard sets `process.exitCode = run(...)` (never `process.exit`, which can truncate piped stdout). `--help` short-circuits before any availability probe. **This one is pinned mechanically, not by grep** — `tests/bin-lib/exit-code-conformance.test.js` (#1903) walks every `plugin/bin/**/*.js`, extracts the text each `require.main === module` guard governs, and fails on a direct `process.exit(...)` inside it. Three prior records (#1176, #1313, #1535) each closed one violation of this rule found by a manual sweep that missed another, which is why the sweep was replaced. A new guard needs no registration; a deliberate exception goes in that test's `ALLOWLIST` with its reason stated beside it (today: `bin/hooks.js`, whose stdout is a synchronous `fs.writeSync(1, …)` with nothing pending to flush, and `bin/lib/statusline-wrapper-source.js`, which deliberately hard-stops on a child process's own exit code).
 - **Precisely, the scan reads only a file's *last* `require.main === module` guard, and only the text that guard governs** — `extractGuard` takes the last regex match, then either a balanced `{…}` block or the bare statement up to its `;`. A file may hold more than one guard: `bin/hooks.js` has its Bash prefilter fast path (#3074) ahead of the real entry point at the bottom. The last guard is the entry point, since a guard that short-circuits before it must appear first, so a direct `process.exit(...)` in an earlier guard is not checked. `hooks.js`'s prefilter exit is safe because nothing has been written to stdout yet. An exit placed outside any guard is invisible to the scan in a file that also exports something. `hooks.js`'s allowlist entry covers the entry-point guard's `main(...).then((code) => process.exit(code))`, and `tests/bin-lib/exit-code-conformance.test.js` pins that the scan selects that guard, not the prefilter one.
```

## Deliverables

- [ ] Move one lazy bullet group out of `cli-wrapper-contract.md` into a sibling file in the skill directory, leaving a one-line pointer bullet (the `status-as-data.md` / `run-dir-boundary-guards.md` pattern). The in-process entry contract and conversion proofs (lines 4-5 at 33f635d03, about 5.3 KB) are the candidate, since both additions land there. Do the same for one lazy section of `SKILL.md`.
- [ ] Repoint every reference that names a moved bullet: `git grep -n cli-wrapper-contract -- tests plugin docs .claude`, including `tests/helpers/run-cli.js`'s `CONTRACT` constant and `docs/plugin-structure.md`.
- [ ] Add the two contract rules in the moved group: (a) resolve a relative path argument where `run` consumes it, `path.isAbsolute(p) ? p : path.resolve(deps.cwd(), p)`, so an absolute path never reads cwd; (b) a child that may prompt on a terminal (a release hook, npm publish) gets `stdio: 'inherit'` when `deps.stdout`/`deps.stderr` are `realDeps`' own, and injected io gets a piped capture routed through deps (release-local.js `run()`'s `live` check).
- [ ] Apply the conversion-proofs change above (the `GIT_WORK_TREE` pairing and the cwd-recording stub).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `cli-wrapper-contract.md` and `SKILL.md` each measure at or below `RAIL_BYTES` with `context-cost.js`'s `measuredBytes`, including the additions.
- [ ] `git grep -n -F 'path.isAbsolute(p) ? p : path.resolve(deps.cwd(), p)' -- .claude/skills/gh-api-module-pattern/` and `git grep -n -F 'GIT_WORK_TREE' -- .claude/skills/gh-api-module-pattern/` each print a line.
- [ ] Every `cli-wrapper-contract` reference found by the grep above resolves to a file and a bullet that exist.
- [ ] Full `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

No user-visible change.

## Technical Approach

### Key Files

`tests/helpers/git-fixtures.js` `gitRepo()` builds its template repo with `fixtureGit(['-C', dir, 'init', ...])` and `fixtureGit(['-C', dir, 'commit', '--allow-empty', ...])`. `fixtureGit` spreads caller opts into `execFileSync` and passes no `env`, so each setup git call inherits the ambient process environment. `linkedWorktreeOf` and `harnessWorktreeOf` call `fixtureGit` the same way.

When `GIT_DIR` / `GIT_WORK_TREE` / `GIT_INDEX_FILE` / `GIT_COMMON_DIR` are set (as inside a git hook running `npm test`), an absolute `GIT_DIR` takes precedence over `-C`, so `init`/`commit`/`worktree add` act on the repo those variables name instead of the fixture dir. - [ ] One regression test in the git-fixtures suite: with `GIT_DIR` in `process.env` naming a different repo, `gitRepo()` creates its init commit in the fixture repo and leaves the `GIT_DIR` repo untouched.

groups.body:
Surface: infra

**Related:** #4931, #4442, #4243, #3822

## Current State

In one worktree-isolated `/flow` run (plugin 6.158.1, Windows Git Bash), the harness's worktree-isolation guard refused 29 Bash calls, logged as `wd-guard-refusal` with `reason: harness-worktree-isolation`, all `actor: session`. Each one was retried as a plain command. The refused shapes were:

- `mkdir -p "<screenshot dir>" && playwright-cli …`, about 14 times during `/test`'s QA run
- `cd "<worktree>" && …` prefixes
- heredocs piped into `python -` / `node -` for small file edits
- a `PW() { "<node.exe>" "<playwright-cli.js>" "$@"; }` shell-function wrapper around the playwright-cli entry point

Most of the guidance this record asked for is now owned by other ready records:

- **QA story agents** (`plugin/agents/qa-agent.md`, both `plugin/skills/test/qa-prompts.md` templates, including their `cd "{ABSOLUTE_WORKTREE_PATH}" && ...` instruction at lines 98 and 162, the per-step `mkdir`, and shell-function wrappers): #4931.
- **`/build`'s Working Directory Discipline**, which still tells dispatchers to require `cd "$WORKTREE" && …` (`plugin/skills/build/SKILL.md:216`): #4442.
- **`/build`'s SDD implementer and reviewer prompts**: #4243.
- **The dispatch-prompt "one plain command per call" mandate**, checked against `_shared/scratch-worktree.md` §7: #3822.

What none of them covers is the orchestrating session itself, the main `/test` session that the `actor: session` events came from:

- `plugin/skills/test/qa-procedures.md`'s Phase 1 step 10 (lines 71-76) tells the orchestrator to generate the QA run directory as a shell assignment of a relative path, `RUN_DIR=".claude-tweaks/artifacts/screenshots/qa/{YYYYMMDD}_{HHMMSS}_{6-char-random-hex}"`. Step 11 (lines 77-79) builds each story's `SCREENSHOT_PATH` from it. That steers the session toward `"$RUN_DIR/…"` paths and `mkdir … &&` chains. It also contradicts `qa-prompts.md:9`, which requires `{SCREENSHOT_PATH}` to be absolute before substitution.
- Neither `plugin/skills/test/SKILL.md` nor `qa-procedures.md` tells the orchestrating session about the worktree shell constraint. `/test`'s verification text already uses "one plain command" for `verify.js` (`plugin/skills/test/verification.md:36`, `:60`), but the QA orchestration phases have no such rule. Nothing there steers small edits to `Edit`/`Write` instead of heredocs, or rules out wrapping `playwright-cli` in a shell function.
- `tests/qa-artifact-path-conformance.test.js:19` pins the literal `RUN_DIR="<prefix>/"` construction text.

## Deliverables

1. Replace `qa-procedures.md`'s Phase 1 step 10 fence with one plain command that prints the run directory as an absolute path under the main checkout's `.claude-tweaks/artifacts/screenshots/qa/` (the existing `node -e` generator, made absolute). Have the orchestrator paste the printed value literally into every later use: step 11's `SCREENSHOT_PATH`, the report paths, and the dispatch substitutions. No shell variable carries it.
2. Add one short orchestrator rule to `qa-procedures.md`, stated once near Phase 1 and cited from `test/SKILL.md`'s QA entry. In a worktree-isolated session, the orchestrating session runs one plain command per Bash call with literal absolute paths, with no `&&`/`;` chain, no `cd … &&`, no shell function, and no heredoc. It uses `Edit`/`Write` for file content, or `Write`s a script file and runs it with one plain command. Cite `_shared/scratch-worktree.md` §7 for the refused shapes rather than restating them.
3. Update `tests/qa-artifact-path-conformance.test.js` so it still pins the `.claude-tweaks/artifacts/screenshots/qa` prefix against the new construction text, and add an assertion that the step 10 fence assigns no shell variable.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `qa-procedures.md`'s step 10 no longer contains a `RUN_DIR=` shell assignment. Its construction prints an absolute path, and steps 11 onward refer to the printed literal value.
- The orchestrator rule from Deliverable 2 appears once in `qa-procedures.md` and is cited (not restated) from `test/SKILL.md`. It names chains, `cd … &&`, shell functions, and heredocs as excluded, and cites `scratch-worktree.md` §7.
- `tests/qa-artifact-path-conformance.test.js` passes against the new text, still asserts the artifacts prefix, and goes red when a `RUN_DIR=` assignment is reintroduced in step 10 (shown by reverting the fence).
- No file that #4931 owns (`qa-agent.md`, `qa-prompts.md`, `scratch-worktree.md`) is edited by this record.
- `npm test` passes, including `tests/qa-prompts-step-origin.test.js` and `tests/test-skill-qa-stamp-conformance.test.js`, which also read `qa-procedures.md`.

## Release Note

The QA orchestrator now runs one plain command per shell call in a worktree session and builds screenshot paths as literal absolute paths, so its setup steps stop getting refused and retried.

## Technical Approach

This is a prose change in `qa-procedures.md` and a one-line citation in `test/SKILL.md`, plus a test update. The guard belongs to Claude Code, so procedure text is the only lever. Keep the absolute-path generator a single `node -e` call (no `$(...)`, no `git` text in the script). Resolve the main checkout root the way `_shared/pipeline-run-dir.md` resolves `$RUN_ROOT`, so the path never lands inside the worktree by accident.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/test/qa-procedures.md` — Phase 1 step 10 absolute-path generation with literal reuse; the orchestrator one-plain-command rule
- `plugin/skills/test/SKILL.md` — cite the orchestrator rule from the QA entry
- `tests/qa-artifact-path-conformance.test.js` — re-pin the prefix against the new construction; assert no shell-variable assignment

## Gotchas

- Scope is the orchestrating session only. The QA story agents and both `qa-prompts.md` templates belong to #4931, and `/build`'s dispatch text belongs to #4442 and #4243. Editing those files here would collide with their builds.
- The run directory path is consumed far downstream (`qa-reporting.md`'s `report.json` `run_dir`, the `retry={RUN_DIR}` re-run hint, `qa-stamp.js --report "{RUN_DIR}/report.json"`). Making it absolute changes what `report.json` records and what the retry hint prints. Check `bin/qa-report.js` and `retry=` parsing (`qa-procedures.md` step 1, which reads `{RETRY_RUN_DIR}/report.json`) still work with an absolute path.
- `.claude-tweaks/artifacts/` must resolve under the main checkout, not the cwd worktree, the same shadowing hazard `_shared/pipeline-run-dir.md` documents for run dirs (`[IL-127]`). An absolute path built from `process.cwd()` inside a worktree would land in the wrong tree.
- ASSUMPTION — verify at build: the `PW() { … }` wrapper in this record's evidence suggests `playwright-cli` was not directly invocable from Git Bash on Windows, so the session built its own launcher. Confirm with `npx --no-install playwright-cli --version` (`plugin/skills/browse/playwright-cli-reference.md:108`) on a Windows Git Bash checkout. If it fails, that launcher gap is a separate defect for a capture, not part of this prose change.

## Original request

test: QA and build procedures compose compound Bash commands the worktree-isolation guard refuses

**Summary:** QA and build procedures build compound Bash commands (`&&` chains, `cd … &&`, heredocs, shell functions) that the harness's worktree-isolation guard refuses, so each one has to be retried as a plain command.

**Kind:** Gap

**Affected component:** /claude-tweaks:test (QA story execution), plus other procedures that compose shell commands, under worktree isolation

**Related:** #4243 (the same shell constraint for /build's SDD dispatch prompts; these refusals came from the main session following /test's own procedure text), #3822

**Use case:**
In one `/flow` run inside a worktree-isolated session (Windows, Git Bash), the harness's worktree-isolation guard refused 29 Bash calls. `friction-events.js` logged them as `wd-guard-refusal`, `reason: harness-worktree-isolation`. Almost all of them used a few compound shapes:
- `mkdir -p <screenshot dir> && <playwright-cli …>`, once for each QA story step's screenshot folder (about 14 refusals during `/test`'s QA run);
- `cd "<worktree>" && …` prefixes;
- heredocs piped into `python -` / `node -` for small file edits;
- shell functions (`PW() { … }`) wrapping the playwright-cli entry point.

Each one had to be retried as a single plain command. The run still worked, but these refusals were its biggest source of friction.

What is wanted: when the session is worktree-isolated, the procedures should tell the agent to issue one plain command per Bash call. For example, create screenshot directories in a separate call (or let the QA tooling create them), run commands from the working directory without `cd … &&`, and use the Edit/Write tools or a scratch script file for edits instead of heredocs. The QA story runner could also create its own screenshot directory, so no `mkdir … &&` prefix is needed at all.

**Evidence:**
- 29 `wd-guard-refusal` events in a single run, all `actor: session`, between the build and test phases.
- Example refused shapes: `mkdir -p ".claude-tweaks/artifacts/screenshots/qa/<run>/<session>/<story>" && …`, `cd "<worktree>" && python - <<'EOF' …`, `PW() { "<node.exe>" "<playwright-cli.js>" "$@"; }; PW …`.
- Cost: about 29 retried tool calls in one run.

**Definition:** Clear

**Plugin version:** 6.158.1

groups.body:
Surface: infra

**Related:** #4990, #4243, #4898

## Current State

Claude Code's worktree-isolation guard refuses Bash calls it cannot verify stay inside the worktree. That guard belongs to the harness, not a plugin hook. In a worktree-isolated `/claude-tweaks:test` QA run on plugin 6.160.0, it refused 13 story-step calls, and each one had to be retried in a plainer form. The refused shapes were:

- a shell variable holding the screenshot directory, used as `playwright-cli … screenshot --filename="$SD/…"`
- `$PWD` inside `--filename`
- a `for n in …; do playwright-cli … screenshot …; done` loop over step names
- a `playwright-cli … | head -5` pipeline

#4990 reports the same failure class from another worktree-isolated run (6.158.1, Windows Git Bash): 29 refusals, about 14 of them `mkdir -p <screenshot dir> && playwright-cli …`, plus `cd "<worktree>" && …` prefixes and a `PW() { … }` shell-function wrapper around the playwright-cli entry point. Each refusal is logged as a `wd-guard-refusal` event (`plugin/bin/lib/hooks/post-tool-use-failure.js:27`, reason `harness-worktree-isolation`), so a clean QA run reads as a noisy one in `friction-events.js`.

The QA prose steers agents toward these shapes:

- Both dispatch templates in `plugin/skills/test/qa-prompts.md` (the structured prompt at line 98 and the legacy prompt at line 162) tell the agent to start every shell command with `cd "{ABSOLUTE_WORKTREE_PATH}" && ...`. That turns every step into a compound call.
- `plugin/agents/qa-agent.md` gives the screenshot and trace directories as placeholders (`{SCREENSHOT_PATH}`, `{TRACES_BASE}`, lines 22-23 and 55-61). The `mkdir -p` calls and the per-step `screenshot --filename={SCREENSHOT_PATH}/<NN>_<step-name>.png` (line 140) say nothing about passing the substituted literal path rather than building it in a shell variable.
- The failure-path trace relocation ("move the freshly-written trace file (the most recently modified one there…)", `qa-prompts.md:132`, `qa-agent.md` Section 6 Step 1) invites a `ls -t … | head -1` plus `mv` chain.
- Neither file mentions the worktree shell constraint. `qa-prompts.md:9` already resolves `{SCREENSHOT_PATH}` and `{TRACES_BASE}` to absolute paths before substitution, so the literal paths are available. Nothing tells the agent to use them verbatim.

`plugin/skills/_shared/scratch-worktree.md` §7 ("Shell constraint", line 235) is the plugin's canonical table of guard-refused shapes. Some of its rows contradict these observations. Its `for` / `while` loop row and its `|` pipeline row both read `passes`, last verified 2026-10-20 (#3340), and it has no row for a `playwright-cli` command carrying a runtime variable, `$PWD`, a loop, a pipe, or a shell-function wrapper. The §7 table itself notes that the guard's boundary moves between builds.

## Deliverables

1. In both dispatch templates in `plugin/skills/test/qa-prompts.md`, replace the `cd "{ABSOLUTE_WORKTREE_PATH}" && ...` instruction with a worktree shell rule. Each Bash call is one plain `playwright-cli` (or `mkdir`/`mv`) command. Use the literal absolute paths the prompt already substitutes for `{SCREENSHOT_PATH}` and `{TRACES_BASE}`. No shell variables, `$PWD`, loops, pipes, `&&`/`;` chains, or shell functions. The working-directory anchor stays as information (the absolute path), not as a `cd` prefix.
2. Add the same rule to `plugin/agents/qa-agent.md` as one short section the Setup, step, and Failure Handling procedures cite. State explicitly that the screenshot `--filename` is the substituted literal `{SCREENSHOT_PATH}/<NN>_<step-name>.png`, written out in full per call, and that each `mkdir -p` is its own call.
3. Rewrite the trace-relocation instruction (`qa-prompts.md:132` and the matching `qa-agent.md` Section 6 Step 1, plus the legacy template's line 180) as two plain calls: list the `.playwright-cli/traces/` directory in one call, then `mv` the chosen file to the literal `{TRACES_BASE}/{story.id}/…` path in a second call.
4. Live-verify the shapes in a worktree-isolated session and record them in `plugin/skills/_shared/scratch-worktree.md` §7. Cover `playwright-cli` with a runtime-variable `--filename`, with `$PWD`, inside a `for` loop, piped into `head`, wrapped in a shell function, and chained after `mkdir -p`. Update the existing `for`-loop and pipeline rows if they no longer pass, with the verified date and this record's number.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `grep -n 'cd "{ABSOLUTE_WORKTREE_PATH}" &&' plugin/skills/test/qa-prompts.md` returns nothing.
- Both QA dispatch templates and `plugin/agents/qa-agent.md` state the one-plain-command-per-call rule, naming variables, `$PWD`, loops, pipes, chains, and shell functions as excluded, and instructing literal absolute paths for screenshots and traces.
- The trace-relocation instruction in both templates and the agent definition is two separate plain calls, with no pipe and no chain.
- `scratch-worktree.md` §7 carries a row for each shape in Deliverable 4. Each row has a live-verified verdict, its refusal wording when refused, and a dated record reference. The existing `for`-loop and pipeline rows match what this build observed.
- A worktree-isolated `/claude-tweaks:test qa` run against at least one story records zero `wd-guard-refusal` events with `actor` naming the QA agent. If no story suite is available, the build reports that this AC could not be exercised rather than marking it met.
- `npm test` passes, including `tests/qa-prompts-step-origin.test.js`, `tests/subagent-contract-clauses.test.js`, and `tests/qa-report-writer-conformance.test.js`, which read these files.

## Release Note

QA story agents now run one plain command per shell call in a worktree session, so their screenshot and trace steps stop getting refused and retried.

## Technical Approach

This is a prose change in two places, plus a measurement. The guard is part of Claude Code, so no plugin code can change what it accepts. The plugin's PreToolUse normalizer (`plugin/bin/lib/hooks/guard-rewrite.js`, described in `scratch-worktree.md` §7's closing paragraph) already rewrites five shapes, but a loop, a pipe, or a shell function is not one of them. So guidance in the prompt the agent actually reads is the fix.

Keep the rule in the dispatch template itself. `qa-prompts.md`'s own contract (line 7) says each template is copied wholesale into the agent's prompt and the agent never sees sibling files, so a pointer to `scratch-worktree.md` would not reach it. State the rule once in each template and once in `qa-agent.md`, and do not restate the §7 table there.

Do the §7 measurement from a worktree-isolated session, one shape per call, recording the guard's exact refusal wording.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/test/qa-prompts.md` — replace the `cd … &&` working-directory instruction in both templates with the one-plain-command rule; split the trace relocation into two calls
- `plugin/agents/qa-agent.md` — add the worktree shell rule; literal-path screenshot and `mkdir` instructions; two-call trace relocation
- `plugin/skills/_shared/scratch-worktree.md` — §7 rows for the `playwright-cli` shapes; re-verify the `for`-loop and pipeline rows

## Gotchas

- #4990 overlaps heavily. It reports the `mkdir -p … &&`, `cd … &&`, and shell-function shapes from the same QA layer, against the same two files. This record covers those QA-layer shapes so the two never edit `qa-prompts.md`/`qa-agent.md` in parallel. #4990's remaining scope (any non-QA `/test` procedure text, such as heredoc-driven file edits) should be narrowed to exclude what lands here.
- #4243 carries the same constraint into `/build`'s SDD dispatch prompts. That is a different file set, and this record does not touch it.
- Do not drop the working-directory anchor. The `cd` prefix existed so screenshots, traces, and git operations land in the right checkout (`qa-prompts.md:98`). Literal absolute paths keep that guarantee without the chain, but any relative path left in the templates (the `.claude-tweaks/auth-state/<vault-name>.json` `state-load` argument, `.playwright-cli/traces/`) then resolves against the agent's actual cwd. Make each one absolute, or confirm the agent's cwd is the worktree.
- The §7 rows are "last observed, not a guarantee". The 2026-10-20 `passes` rows and this record's refusals may both be right for their builds. Record what this build observes, with a date. Never delete a row to make the table agree.
- `qa-prompts.md:92` requires the two templates and `qa-agent.md` to stay in sync for the `REPORT_JSON` schema. This change does not touch that schema, but edit both templates the same way so they stay parallel.
- Windows Git Bash (#4990's environment) may refuse a different set of shapes. Note the platform on each §7 row.

## Original request

qa-agent: story steps get refused in a worktree-isolated session when they use shell variables, loops or pipes

**Related:** #4898

**Summary:** QA story steps get refused in a worktree-isolated session when they use shell variables, loops or pipes.

**Kind:** Gap

**Affected component:** qa-agent

**Use case:**
During a `/claude-tweaks:test` QA run in a session isolated in a git worktree, 13 Bash calls for story steps were refused by Claude Code's worktree-isolation guard ("Refusing to run it"), and each step had to be retried in a plainer form. The refused calls had these shapes:

- a shell variable holding the screenshot directory, then `playwright-cli ... screenshot --filename="$SD/..."`
- `$PWD` inside `--filename`
- a `for n in ...; do playwright-cli ... screenshot ...; done` loop over step names
- a `playwright-cli ... | head -5` pipeline

`friction-events.js` logs each one as `wd-guard-refusal`, so a clean QA run reads as a noisy one, and every refusal costs a retry. The refusal comes from the harness guard, not a plugin hook, so the fix is guidance: say in the QA dispatch prompt and the qa-agent definition that a worktree-isolated session takes one plain `playwright-cli` command per Bash call, with literal absolute paths and no variables, loops or pipes, and spell out the screenshot path in the prompt so the agent has no reason to build it in the shell. `_shared/scratch-worktree.md` §7 is the natural home for the table row.

**Definition:** Clear

**Plugin version:** 6.160.0

Surface: infra

**Related:** #4861, #644, #4462, #4960

## Current State

Reconcile has failed `removal-failed` on `.claude/worktrees/flow-spec-4738` since 2026-11-01. The worktree is locked with reason `claude session flow-spec-4738 (pid 3588 start Sat Oct 31 14:21:07 2026)`. As of 2026-11-02 the worktree is clean (`git status --porcelain` prints nothing) and its PR #4863 merged on 2026-11-01, so nothing in it needs keeping.

The lock is stale through pid reuse. pid 3588 is alive, but it is now `/usr/libexec/gamecontrolleragentd`, started Mon Nov 2 06:22:00 2026, not the Claude session the lock names. `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/worktree-reap.js`'s `lockVerdict` (around line 154) calls `isPidAlive(entry.pid)`, which only checks that some process holds the pid (`process.kill(pid, 0)`), so the worktree reads `in-use` indefinitely. The function's own comment accepts this as under-reaping ("a recycled pid reads as alive and the worktree is skipped"). The lock reason already records the holder's start time, and `parseWorktreeList` (the `PID_RE` at line 27) reads the pid from it but discards the start time.

Sibling record #4861 had the same shape for `review-v6158-fixes`. That one resolved on its own because its pid (11546) exited and was not reused, which shows the stuck case depends only on whether the OS happens to recycle the pid.

## Deliverables

1. Remove the stuck worktree once: confirm it is still clean and #4863 is still merged, then `git worktree unlock` and `git worktree remove` `.claude/worktrees/flow-spec-4738`, and delete its `worktree-flow-spec-4738` branch with `git branch -d` (or `-D` only with the merged-PR proof).
2. In `worktree-reap.js`, parse the start time from the lock reason alongside the pid. In `lockVerdict`, when a start time was recorded and the live pid's start time can be read and differs from it, return `orphaned` instead of `in-use`.
3. Keep fail-closed behavior: a lock with no recorded start time, a start time that does not parse, or a live process whose start time cannot be read stays `in-use`, exactly as today.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `.claude/worktrees/flow-spec-4738` no longer appears in `git worktree list`.
- A unit test with a lock reason naming pid P and start time S, where P is alive with a different start time, gets `orphaned`. The same lock with a matching start time gets `in-use`.
- Unit tests pin each fail-closed case from Deliverable 3 as `in-use`.
- The existing `ORPHAN_GRACE_MS` / `isStale()` gate still applies before any `orphaned` worktree is reaped. This record changes the liveness verdict only, not the reap policy.
- `npm test` passes, including the Windows CI job (where reading a pid's start time may be unavailable and must fall back to `in-use`).

## Release Note

The worktree reaper no longer treats a stale session lock as live just because the operating system reused its process id.

## Technical Approach

Extend `parseWorktreeList` to capture the `start {date}` text after the pid and store it on the entry (for example `lockStartedAt`). Read the live process's start time through an injectable seam (on macOS and Linux, `ps -o lstart= -p {pid}`; on Windows, return unknown), so tests never shell out. Compare at second resolution. Any read or parse failure returns unknown, and unknown means `in-use`. The reap decision downstream (`isStale`, the grace window, the dirty check) is unchanged.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/worktree-reap.js` — parse the lock start time; start-time-aware `lockVerdict`
- `tests/hooks-worktree-reap.test.js` — verdict cases for reused, matching, and unreadable start times

## Gotchas

- Do not drop the `isPidAlive` check. A dead pid stays `orphaned` exactly as now; the start-time comparison only adds a second way to reach `orphaned` when the pid is alive.
- `ps -o lstart` prints local time in a fixed format; the lock reason's date is written by the session that took the lock. Compare both as parsed timestamps, never as strings, and treat a timezone or format mismatch as unknown.
- Deliverable 1 is a one-time operational step in the main checkout. Run it before or after the code change, but verify cleanliness and the merged PR at the moment of removal, not from this record's snapshot.
- `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/reap-merged.test.js` and `tests/run-liveness-callers-conformance.test.js` also reference `lockVerdict`; run them, since a verdict change can shift their fixtures.

groups.body:
Surface: infra

**Related:** #4895, #644, #4960, #4209

## Current State

Reconcile escalated `removal-failed` three passes in a row on `.claude/worktrees/review-v6158-fixes`. Git refused the removal because the worktree was locked (`claude session review-v6158-fixes (pid 11546 …)`). That PR (#4823) had already merged on 2026-11-01. On 2026-11-11 the path is gone: `git worktree list --porcelain` no longer lists it, and the directory does not exist. Its `removal-failed` entry is also gone from `.claude-tweaks/reconcile-cache.json`'s `residueFailures`, but this record is still open. `pruneResidueFailures` (`plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/cache.js:419`) drops the entry of a vanished path even when closing the filed issue fails, and leaves that issue for a human to close (`cache.js:414-416`). So the operational handoff this record was filed for no longer applies.

The underlying defect is still live. Every locked worktree whose lock is not held by a live pid gets the same guaranteed escalation:

- `reapMerged` (`plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/reap-merged.js:230`) skips a candidate only when `isWorktreeLocked(real, { cwd: root })` is true.
- `isWorktreeLocked` (`plugin/bin/lib/hooks/worktree-reap.js:406-418`) returns `lockVerdict(entry) === 'in-use'`. A lock whose pid is dead (`'orphaned'`) or whose reason names no pid (`'unknown'`, `worktree-reap.js:153-157`) reads as not locked.
- `reapMerged` then runs a plain `git worktree remove` (`reap-merged.js:251`). Git always refuses that for a locked worktree, so the candidate lands in `removal-failed` (`reap-merged.js:270`). After `RESIDUE_ESCALATE_THRESHOLD` passes it is filed as a record like this one.
- The sibling reaper `reapWorktrees` handles the same verdicts deliberately (`worktree-reap.js:289-297` and `:314`). It skips `'unknown'` ("lock reason unrecognized") and skips an `'orphaned'` worktree still inside `ORPHAN_GRACE_MS` (24h, `worktree-reap.js:60`). It runs `git worktree unlock` before removing an `'orphaned'` worktree that has passed the grace window. `reapMerged` has neither guard.
- `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/reap-merged.test.js:304-335` depends on this defect. Its removal-failed streak test forces the failure by locking the fixture worktree with a pid-less reason, so the `'unknown'` lock reads as free and the plain removal fails.

This record's own lock reason named pid 11546, so its verdict was `'orphaned'` (a dead pid) and not `'in-use'`. An `'in-use'` verdict would have skipped the worktree at line 230 before any removal was attempted.

## Deliverables

1. In `reapMerged`, replace the `isWorktreeLocked` gate with the `lockVerdict` decision `reapWorktrees` already applies, reading the verdict from the `parseWorktreeList` entry the loop already holds:
   - `'in-use'` — skip with reason `in-use`, unchanged.
   - `'unknown'` — skip with a quiet, distinct reason (no removal attempt, no residue streak).
   - `'orphaned'` within `ORPHAN_GRACE_MS` (by `isStale(real, now)`) — skip with a distinct reason (no removal attempt, no residue streak).
   - `'orphaned'` past the grace window — run `git worktree unlock` on the path, then the existing plain `git worktree remove` (never `--force`). The existing long-path fallback and `removal-failed` escalation stay unchanged for a removal that still fails.
   - `'free'` — unchanged.
2. Add every new skip reason that fires on each background pass for a healthy state (the grace-window skip) to the quiet set `reapMerged` already consults, so it does not log a `worktree-reap-skipped` event on every pass.
3. Rework every `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/reap-merged.test.js` test that forces a removal failure by locking its fixture with the pid-less reason `'stuck'` (the `git worktree lock … --reason stuck` calls at lines 313, 344, 369-370, 410, 759, 818, and 857). Force the failure through a mechanism that still fails after this change. For example, use a modified tracked file in the worktree, which a plain `git worktree remove` refuses. Any test whose subject is the locked-tree refusal itself (the `attemptLongPathRemoval` win32 cases near lines 756 and 815) may keep a lock, but it must be one the new branch still sends to removal (a stale, dead-pid lock) or call the function directly. It must not depend on an `'unknown'` lock reaching `git worktree remove`.
4. Add unit tests for `reapMerged` covering each verdict branch from Deliverable 1.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A merged-PR worktree locked with a pid-less reason is skipped with no `git worktree remove` attempt, and leaves no `removal-failed` entry in `residueFailures` after `RESIDUE_ESCALATE_THRESHOLD` passes.
- A merged-PR worktree locked by a dead pid, modified within `ORPHAN_GRACE_MS`, is skipped with no removal attempt and no residue entry.
- A merged-PR worktree locked by a dead pid, untouched past `ORPHAN_GRACE_MS` and clean, is reaped: unlocked, removed, and listed in `reaped`.
- A merged-PR worktree locked by a live pid is still skipped as `in-use`.
- The reworked removal-failed streak test still reaches `escalated: true` at the threshold, and its failure comes from a mechanism other than a worktree lock.
- `node --test tests/bin-lib/reconcile/reap-merged.test.js tests/reconcile.test.js tests/hooks-worktree-reap.test.js` passes, and so does the full `npm test`.

## Release Note

Stop the background reconcile pass from repeatedly filing removal-failed records for merged worktrees that a crashed or exited session left locked.

## Technical Approach

Import `lockVerdict`, `isStale`, and `ORPHAN_GRACE_MS` (already exported from `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/worktree-reap.js`) into `reap-merged.js`. Then branch on `lockVerdict(wt)` inside the loop, in place of the `isWorktreeLocked` call. `wt` is the `parseWorktreeList` entry the loop already iterates, so no second `git worktree list` call is needed. That also drops one fork per candidate. Mirror `reapWorktrees`' existing order and wording (`worktree-reap.js:289-297`, `:314`) so the two reapers keep one lock policy, not two. Run the unlock only immediately before the removal, after `decideReap` has confirmed the PR merged and the dry-run return, so a dry run still writes nothing (#4180). Keep the `isOwnCwd` guard ahead of the lock branch (#644).

`teardown-run.js:231` also calls `isWorktreeLocked`, but it is a different consumer with its own semantics and stays out of scope.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/reap-merged.js` — replace the `isWorktreeLocked` gate with the `lockVerdict` branch; unlock a stale orphaned worktree before removal
- `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/reap-merged.test.js` — rework the lock-based removal-failed fixture; add the per-verdict cases
- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/worktree-reap.js` — read only, unless an export is missing (`lockVerdict`, `isStale`, `ORPHAN_GRACE_MS`, `QUIET_SKIP_REASONS` are exported today)

## Gotchas

- Never add `--force` to the removal. After the unlock, a plain `git worktree remove` still refuses a worktree with modified tracked files, and that refusal is the remaining safety net for uncommitted work. It must still surface as `removal-failed`.
- The #1341 test (around `reap-merged.test.js:353`) pins git's real stderr as `lastError` and today expects the "cannot remove a locked working tree" text. When the fixture switches to the new failure mechanism, update that assertion to the new mechanism's real git stderr. Never hand-type it: capture it from an actual `git worktree remove` run.
- `'orphaned'` alone is not proof the worktree is finished: a resumed session carries a new pid while its lock keeps the old one (`worktree-reap.js:46-54`). The `isStale` grace check is what protects that case, so do not drop it.
- #4895 changes `lockVerdict` itself, to read a pid-reused lock as `'orphaned'`. This record consumes `lockVerdict` unchanged and takes no position on that change. If #4895 lands first, its newly `'orphaned'` locks flow through this record's grace-window and unlock path, which is the intended composition. #4895's own Current State says its worktree "reads `in-use` indefinitely". But its record carries the same `removal-failed`/"cannot remove a locked working tree" error, which only happens when `isWorktreeLocked` returned false. So it is likely also an instance of this record's defect, worth a look when either one builds.
- ASSUMPTION — verify at build: this record stayed open because the vanished path's resolve call in `pruneResidueFailures` failed or returned a non-closing status, and the entry was dropped anyway. That drop-on-failure posture is #4209's subject, not this record's. Confirm via #4209 and a fresh `node plugin/bin/hooks.js reconcile` report. This record closes through its own PR either way.

## Original request

**Reason:** `removal-failed`
**Last error:** fatal: cannot remove a locked working tree, lock reason: claude session review-v6158-fixes (pid 11546 start Sat Oct 31 16:00:39 2026)
use 'remove -f -f' to override or unlock first

**Dirty files (`git status --porcelain` at the last failed pass):**
```
```

Only `??` (untracked) entries that are plainly disposable make `git worktree remove --force /Users/thomasholknielsen/Code Workspaces/claude-tweaks/.claude/worktrees/review-v6158-fixes` safe; any modified tracked entry means inspect first.

## Current State

`findRecentCommitOverlap` in `plugin/bin/lib/issues/recent-commit-check.js` matches words from a new record's title against commit subjects from the last 14 days, and posts a triage comment on two or more shared words. On 2026-11-01 it commented on 12 of 14 new records: 10 matched only template words (`settle`, `digest`, `findings`, plus the area name), and 2 matched `pr-scan` and `item`. Passing files makes it worse, because the threshold drops to one word: #4809 went from 12 hits to 17.

History is equally weak. Of 82 records carrying the comment, 2 closed as not planned (#1970, #1776). How many of the 54 completed ones were already fixed is unmeasured, and #1316's own requirement of a low false-positive rate was never measured.

The comment sets no label, so a true match does not stop a build either. `_shared/health-recent-commit-check.md` still calls it a gap-closer for the #1068 failure, where a record is built after its fix has already merged.

## Deliverables

- The screen asks whether the flawed code still exists. It extracts a record's anchors (the file:line references and quoted symbols in Current State, reusing `near-duplicate.js`'s anchor extraction where it fits), and tests them at `HEAD` and against commits in the lookback window touching those files.
- A rollup record (a digest cluster) tests each entry's anchor and flags only entries whose anchor is gone.
- A confirmed match sets `needs:decision` with a proposal naming the commit and the missing anchor, so the record does not build until a human answers. A weak or unprovable result posts nothing, and a failed screen still never blocks filing.
- A record with no anchors gets no comment: no evidence means no signal.
- The open-PR screen stops matching on title words alone: it requires a shared Key File or anchor.
- A replay tool run over the 82 existing records states measured precision in the PR body.
- `health-recent-commit-check.md` and all five filing call sites describe the new behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A test proves a record whose anchor still exists at `HEAD` gets no comment and no label, even when commit subjects share its title words.
- A test proves a record whose anchored line was removed by a commit in the window gets `needs:decision` naming that commit.
- A test proves a rollup flags only the entries whose anchors are gone.
- Replaying the fixture of #4807's title and Key Files produces no match.
- A test proves a git failure or an anchorless record yields no comment and no filing failure.
- The PR body quotes the replay's output over the 82 records.

## Release Note

Flag a new record only when the code it describes has really changed, and hold that record until someone confirms it.

## Technical Approach

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/issues/recent-commit-check.js` — modify
- `plugin/skills/_shared/health-recent-commit-check.md` — modify
- `plugin/bin/lib/issues/near-duplicate.js` — modify
- `plugin/skills/capture/SKILL.md` — modify
- `plugin/skills/code-health/filing.md` — modify
- `plugin/skills/harness-health/filing.md` — modify
- `plugin/skills/docs-health/SKILL.md` — modify
- `plugin/skills/journey-health/SKILL.md` — modify

_Filed by `capture` via specShapedBody._

## Decisions

Plan-review answers (2026-11-02). The governing rule is this record's own: a weak or unprovable signal posts nothing. Apply it to any further anchor-classification question rather than stopping on it.

- **Line references: HEAD numbering.** A `file:line` reference is judged at `HEAD`. An in-range line counts as live. Only a missing file, or a line past the end of the file with a removing commit in the window, counts as gone. Line numbers drift too easily to prove more than that.
- **Bare paths: context only.** A path that still exists casts no vote either way, and the decision comment never claims that no anchors remain.
- **Stub captures: screened at shaping.** A stub has no anchors at filing, so `/specify` runs the screen when it shapes the record. This keeps coverage for the #3191 duplicate-of-open-PR case, and the journey is rewritten to say so.
- **`relfile#Symbol` anchors** count as symbol anchors in that file.
- **Rollups.** A rollup's proposal stays single-line for its single-line readers, naming the flagged entries' count and first entry, with the full list in the comment body.
- **Dispatch holds on `needs:*`.** `dispatch/queue-pull-script.md`'s eligibility filter excludes a record with any `needs:*` label, so a confirmed match really does stop the build. A test covers this, with a report line that names the label.
- **Plan shape.** Task 1 exports the anchor classifier that Task 2 uses. Tasks 2 and 3 carry `**Review risk:** high`.

groups.body:
Origin: spec #4578 review (3e Architecture, tiebreak-confirmed)

Defer-reason: genuinely-larger

## Current State

Record #4578 made forge detection (`detectIntegrationModel`, `plugin/bin/lib/policy-schema.js`) honour `gh-timeout-ms`, retry once on a timeout, and report a *degraded* detection (a timeout that survives the retry) through an opt-in `onDegrade` callback, distinct from a detected `local-merge`. The callers that matter for pipeline correctness consume it (`resolve-policy.js`, the PreToolUse PR-stamp gate, `precondition.js`, the Manifesto, `phase-exit.js`). Two consumer families still treat a degraded detection as a plain `local-merge`:

- `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/index.js` (around line 266) forwards a `timeoutMs` to `resolveIntegrationModel` but wires no `onDegrade`. After a timeout and a failed retry, `reconcile()` takes its non-`pr-first` branch (legacy reap) and records the skip as `reason: 'local-merge-model'` — the same entry a genuinely detected `local-merge` produces — so a degraded SessionStart pass cannot be told apart from a real one. Plan-review Q1 scoped #4578 to the `timeoutMs` forwarding only; the spec Release Note ("reports a degraded detection instead of silently resolving local-merge") is therefore not true on this path.

- `plugin/bin/lib/express/policy.js` (`defaultResolvePolicy`) and `plugin/bin/lib/flow/preflight.js` (`defaultDeps().resolvePolicy`) call `computeDerivedDefaults` without `onDegrade`, and their consumers read only `.value`: `express/cli.js` passes `policy['integration-model'].value` to the eligibility gate, so a degraded detection reads as "integration-model is not pr-first"; `flow/preflight.js` drops the `degraded` field when it builds the lever table. Both fail closed (express is ineligible; the preflight levers are display-only), but neither names the cause.

Verified at the review of #4578 (tiebreak verdicts: confirmed, low severity). Not a regression — before #4578 the same timeout resolved `local-merge` silently with no retry.

## Deliverables

1. `reconcile()` passes an `onDegrade` collector to `resolveIntegrationModel` and carries a degraded detection in its result (for example a distinct skip reason such as `degraded-forge-detection`, or a `degraded` field), so a degraded pass is distinguishable from a detected `local-merge`; the SessionStart consumer surfaces it the way `resolve-policy.js` does (one `degraded —` line).

2. `express/cli.js` reports a degraded `integration-model` as its own ineligibility reason instead of "not pr-first", reading the `degraded` field `computeDerivedDefaults` already writes.

3. `flow/preflight.js`'s lever entries keep the `degraded` field (or the preflight table marks the lever), so the FYI Manifesto table does not present a guess as a detected value.

4. A short statement in `plugin/skills/_shared/forge-detection.md` (Code twin paragraph) of the contract every consumer follows: handle `degraded` or consciously ignore it.

## Acceptance Criteria

With a fake `gh` that always times out, `reconcile()` reports a degraded detection (a result field or skip reason distinct from `local-merge-model`) and a detected `local-merge` (no remote) does not.

With the same fake `gh`, `express-lane.js gate` returns an ineligibility reason that names the degraded forge detection, not "integration-model is not pr-first".

With the same fake `gh`, the preflight `levers` output for `integration-model` carries the degraded marker.

Each new case goes red against the current code. `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

Reconcile, the express lane and the flow preflight now report a degraded forge detection instead of treating it as a detected local-merge.

## Technical Approach

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/index.js` — wire onDegrade, carry the degrade in the result
- `plugin/bin/lib/express/cli.js` — name a degraded detection as its own ineligibility reason
- `plugin/bin/lib/express/policy.js` — forward onDegrade or keep the entry field for the gate
- `plugin/bin/lib/flow/preflight.js` — keep the degraded field on the integration-model lever entry
- `plugin/skills/_shared/forge-detection.md` — state the consumer contract for degraded

_Filed by `review`. Close to resolve; label `wontfix` to suppress future reports of this finding._

## Current State

The stash guard (plugin/bin/stash-guard.js snapshot, compare and restore) wraps only /build's subagent-driven-development dispatches. ## Acceptance Criteria

Surface: backend

**Related:** #4359, #4429, #3974, #4358, #4366, #4395, #4553, #4593, #4708, #4718

## Current State

In a multi-spec `/claude-tweaks:flow` run every record shares one worktree and branch, so a later record's `/claude-tweaks:review` must review only its own commits. `review/code-mode-steps.md` Step 2 derives `{base}` from the integration branch and has no rule for a record's own range inside the shared branch. Nothing records it either: `flow/multispec-run-dir-layout.md`'s `manifest.yml` keeps per-spec status and phase timestamps, with no base sha.

In run 2026-10-31T101111 (8 records) the controller supplied the range by hand as the parent of each record's materialize commit. It built the review context from the wrong base twice (#4070, #4090) before correcting it, each time re-running `build-review-context.js`.

The filer's probe, `git grep -n -i -e "multi-spec" -e "MULTISPEC" -e "materialize commit" origin/main -- plugin/skills/review/code-mode-steps.md plugin/skills/review/step3-lens-dispatch.md plugin/bin/lib/review-context`, matched only the verdict-marker, worktree-entry and prior-review-reuse paragraphs, and no per-record base rule.

## Deliverables

1. Define a record's own review range in a multi-spec shared worktree: `{base}` is the parent of that record's materialize commit (`Materialize spec #{N}`), `{branch}` is `HEAD`.
2. Give review Step 2 that rule under `$MULTISPEC_PARENT_DIR`, and have `/claude-tweaks:flow`'s per-spec review invocation pass the range, or a sha the review reads, instead of leaving it to the controller.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Under `$MULTISPEC_PARENT_DIR`, review Step 2 names the per-record base without the controller computing it.
2. A conformance pin fails if the rule is removed.
3. A single-spec review still derives `{base}` from the integration branch.

## Release Note

Multi-spec `/flow` runs review each record against its own commits automatically.

## Technical Approach

Prefer resolving the sha mechanically from the materialize commit's subject over asking the controller to carry it.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/review/code-mode-steps.md` — Step 2: per-record base under MULTISPEC_PARENT_DIR
- `plugin/skills/flow/multi-spec.md` — pass the per-record range to the per-spec review

## Gotchas

- A resumed series, or a record re-materialized on the same branch, can have more than one matching commit, so the rule must say which one wins.

## Original request

Review a multi-spec record against its own commit range

In a multi-spec `/claude-tweaks:flow` run every record shares one worktree and branch, so a later record's `/claude-tweaks:review` must review only its own commits. `review/code-mode-steps.md` Step 2 derives `{base}` from the integration branch and has no rule for a record's own range inside the shared branch; nothing records it either (`flow/multispec-run-dir-layout.md`: `manifest.yml` keeps per-spec status and phase timestamps, no base sha).

In run 2026-10-31T101111 (8 records) the controller supplied the range by hand as the parent of each record's materialize commit, and built the review context from the wrong base twice (#4070, #4090) before correcting it — each a re-run of `build-review-context.js`.

Probe: `git grep -n -i -e "multi-spec" -e "MULTISPEC" -e "materialize commit" origin/main -- plugin/skills/review/code-mode-steps.md plugin/skills/review/step3-lens-dispatch.md plugin/bin/lib/review-context` — matched only the verdict-marker, worktree-entry and prior-review-reuse paragraphs, no per-record base rule.

## Deliverables

1. Define a record's own review range in a multi-spec shared worktree: `{base}` = the parent of that record's materialize commit (`Materialize spec #{N}`), `{branch}` = `HEAD`.
2. Give review Step 2 that rule under `$MULTISPEC_PARENT_DIR`, and have `/claude-tweaks:flow`'s per-spec review invocation pass the range (or a sha the review reads) instead of leaving it to the controller.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Under `$MULTISPEC_PARENT_DIR`, review Step 2 names the per-record base without the controller computing it.
2. A conformance pin fails if the rule is removed.

## Release Note

Multi-spec `/flow` runs review each record against its own commits automatically.

## Technical Approach

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/review/code-mode-steps.md` — Step 2: per-record base under MULTISPEC_PARENT_DIR
- `plugin/skills/flow/multi-spec.md` — pass the per-record range to the per-spec review
