groups.body:
**Related:** #4303

Origin: wrap-up leftover from #4281

Defer-reason: pre-existing-outside-diff

## Current State

The #4281 differential check (bash 3.2 and 5, 3000 fuzzed commands, base 5fb12cb2c vs the #4281 branch) and its final whole-branch review found these pre-existing gaps in `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/git-command.js`. Each one already existed at base, so #4281 left it alone:
- A literal `$`, backtick or `"` inside a quoted value (`mkdir '$(x)'`, `cp src \"`) yields no target, though bash writes that name. `isUnresolvable` rejects the character even when its span kind is `s` or escaped.
- An escape at a trimmed segment-piece end is lost. An escaped trailing space (`echo x > a\ ; ls`, `cd wt\ && tee a`) and a backslash-newline (`echo x > ab\<newline>; echo y`) are read as a stray `\`. Bash writes `a ` or `ab`. POSIX reports nothing; win32 drops the space.
- `A\=x git commit` reports a spurious git target. `findGitLead` and `powershellOpaqueCommand` still skip assignments with `SIMPLE_ASSIGNMENT_RE` on the value instead of `isAssignmentWord` on the kinds.
- `echo $( [[ x > /main/i ]] )` reports a write target, a spurious deny: bash compares and writes nothing.
- A glued redirect after a word holding a bare `$` is dropped: `x=f1; echo $x>f1` and `x=f1; A=$x>f1` write `f1` in bash 5, and both base and HEAD report nothing. The spaced `echo $x >f1` is reported.
- `>\&2` writes the file `&2`, which is never reported. (The unescaped `>&file` form is #4303's U6.)
- A quoted `$NAME` glued to a bare continuation is read as a longer name: `A=f1; echo x > "$A"g` writes `f1g` in bash 3.2 and 5, and base and HEAD both report nothing (the #4281 review's gap sweep).
- An MSYS spelling of a native path (`/d/repo/x`, which Git Bash maps to `D:\repo\x`) resolves under path.win32 as a drive-less rooted path, so every gate fails open for it on Windows (pre-existing at base; the #4281 review's gap sweep).
- A cd whose argument carries a glued redirect, or a redirect before `cd`, mis-tracks the cwd: `cd sub>f1` resolves the cd to `sub>f1`, `A=x> cd sub` tracks a cd that never runs, and `> f1 cd sub; echo y > f2` reports `/w/f2` where bash writes `sub/f2`.

## Deliverables

- [ ] Accept a literal `$`, backtick or `"` that the span mask shows is quoted or escaped as a path character, and keep an unquoted expansion unresolvable.
- [ ] Keep a trailing escaped space and a backslash-newline at a piece end in the word value (no stray-`\` read).
- [ ] Have `findGitLead` and `powershellOpaqueCommand` reuse `isAssignmentWord` with the span kinds.
- [ ] Start the redirect scan after a `[[ … ]]` nested inside `$( … )`.
- [ ] Read a glued redirect after a word whose bare `$` part is a plain parameter reference.
- [ ] Report the escaped `>\&2` as a write to the file `&2`.
- [ ] Read a quoted `$NAME` followed by a bare continuation as the name plus a literal suffix.
- [ ] Under path.win32, map an MSYS `/x/…` path to `X:\…` before resolving it.
- [ ] Track the cwd for a cd line whose words carry a glued or leading redirect as bash does.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `fileWriteTargets("mkdir '$(x)'", "/wt")` is unaffected, and `fileWriteTargets("cp src 'a$b'", "/m")` reports `/m/a$b`, each pinned with a bash 3.2 and 5 verdict.
2. `fileWriteTargets("echo x > a\\ ; ls", "/m")` reports `/m/a ` under path.posix.
3. `gitTargets("A\\=x git commit -m y", "/wt")` deep-equals `[]`.
4. `fileWriteTargets("echo $( [[ x > /main/i ]] )", "/wt")` deep-equals `[]`.
5. `fileWriteTargets("x=/m/f; echo $x>/m/g", "/wt")` reports `/m/g`, pinned with a bash 3.2 and 5 verdict.
6. `fileWriteTargets("echo x >\\&2", "/m")` reports `/m/&2`, pinned with a bash 3.2 and 5 verdict.
7. `fileWriteTargets("> f1 cd sub; echo y > f2", "/r")` reports `/r/f1` and `/r/sub/f2`.
8. `fileWriteTargets('A=/m/f; echo x > "$A"g', "/w")` reports `/m/fg`, pinned with a bash 3.2 and 5 verdict.
9. Under path.win32 with a cwd `D:\wt`, `fileWriteTargets("echo x > /d/main/a.js", ...)` reports `D:\main\a.js`.
10. The shell-scanner-bash-differential base comparison shows no target lost against the merge base.

## Release Note

The Bash write guards recognise a few more quoted and escaped path shapes exactly as bash reads them, and stop flagging one comparison as a write.

## Technical Approach

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/git-command.js` — kind-aware isUnresolvable, piece-end escape handling, dropRedirections operator kinds, isAssignmentWord reuse, nested [[ in $( )
- `tests/hooks-git-command.test.js` — bash-cited pins for each shape

_Filed by `wrap-up leftover routing` via specShapedBody._

## Absorbed: 2026-10-25 — git -C argument with a glued or spaced redirect

Origin: v6.155.1 release whole-branch review (base v6.155.0), refs #4026. Defer-reason: tangential — pre-dates the release (same behavior at v6.155.0); not a blocker for it.

The same glued-redirect class this record already names for `cd` also bites `git -C`, and a spaced redirect between `-C <dir>` and the subcommand hides the git call entirely. Probed against `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/git-command.js` `gitTargets(cmd, '/wt')` at origin/main 0751b4237:

| Command | `gitTargets` result | Bash's reading |
|---|---|---|
| `git -C /main>/dev/null commit -m x` | `[{action:"commit", dir:"/main>/dev/null"}]` | commit in `/main`, stdout to `/dev/null` |
| `git -C /main >/dev/null commit -m x` | `[]` (commit not detected) | commit in `/main` |
| `cd /main>/dev/null; git commit -m x` (already listed above) | `[{action:"commit", dir:"/main>/dev/null"}]` | commit in `/main` |

- [ ] Strip a glued redirect from a `-C` value the way bash does (`/main>/dev/null` → dir `/main`).
- [ ] Skip redirect words (and their targets) between `git`'s global options and the subcommand, so `git -C /main >/dev/null commit` is detected as a commit in `/main`.
- [ ] Pin each row above as a `gitTargets` test case.

## Absorbed: 2026-11-03 — glued redirect after an escaped blank, the word parts #4294 left out

Origin: build of #4294. Defer-reason: tangential — #4294's Acceptance Criteria name the `$NAME`, `${ … }` and backtick prefixes only, and these shapes need a nesting read a single token does not give.

#4294 made `echo $M\ >x` resolve `x` through `escapedBlankPrefixOk` in `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/git-command.js`. These neighbours still resolve no target where bash 3.2, bash 5 and zsh all write (measured 2026-11-03). Each is pinned in `tests/hooks-gate-coverage.test.js` under an `AC1.1 #4294: … stays a known miss without a target` title, so a fix flips a pin on purpose.

| Command | Shells write | Scanner |
|---|---|---|
| `echo $(d)\ >x`, `echo $((1))\ >x` | x | `[]` |
| `echo $[1]\ >x` | x | `[]` |
| ``echo `d e`\ >x``, a backtick holding a blank | x | `[]` |
| `` echo `$M\ >x` ``, a redirect inside the backtick | x | `[]` |
| `echo "$(a $M\ >x)"`, inside a quoted substitution | x | `[]` |
| `WT=y; echo $M\ >$WT/x`, ``WT=y; echo `d`\ >$WT/x``, a `$VAR` target `substituteVars` skips (a second `$` or a backtick) | y/x | `[]` |
| `echo ${M:-\ }>x` | x | `[]` |
| `` echo $M\ `d`>x ``, a backtick after the last escaped blank | x | `[]` |
| `echo $'\''\ >x`, `echo $'it\'s'\ >x`, an ANSI-C string the tokenizer misreads | x | `[]` |
| `` echo `(d)`\ >x ``, `echo ${M:-$(d)}\ >x`, a `(` inside a closed part | x | `[]` |
| `echo $M"\ ">x`, a quoted blank after a bare `$` part | x | `[]` |
| `echo $M\<CR>>x`, an escaped carriage return | x | `[]` |
| `echo $${M\ >x}` | `x}` in bash only | `[]` |

The reverse direction, on the safe side: an expansion an earlier token opened reads as a false deny, as the plain word does at base. `` echo ${M:-`d}`\ >x} `` gives `x}`, `[[ a && $M\ >x ]]` gives `x`, `echo $[ $M\ >1 ]` gives `1`, `echo $(( $M\ >>1 ))` gives `1`, and `for ((i=0; $M\ >1; i++)); do break; done` gives `1;`; bash writes nothing for any of them. So does `echo $'\'\ >x'`, which gives `x'`: the tokenizer misreads `$'\'` (the spaced `echo $'\' >x'` gives `x'` at base too), so fix it in `tokenize`, not with more prefix rules. 

A chained glued redirect is a leak, not a safe-side read, whenever a later target is protected. `echo foo>ok>/main/leak` and `echo $M\ >ok>/main/leak` both report `{cwd}/ok>/main/leak`, one joined name under the cwd, while the shells write `ok` and `/main/leak`. The first form is pre-existing at base, and the second reads the same way since #4294.

- [ ] Resolve each operator of a chained glued redirect as its own target.
- [ ] Cut a write-shape operand at a bare `>`: `tee a\ >x`, `M=a; tee $M\ >x` and `M=a; cp b $M\ >x` report the operand `a >x` at base and head, where bash ends the word at `>`.

- [ ] Resolve a `$VAR` target after such a word.
- [ ] Each row above resolves the target the shells write, pinned with a bash 3.2 and 5 verdict, and #4294's known-miss pins are updated in the same change.

**Related:** #4138, #3972

Origin: build #4138 (final whole-branch review, Minor 8)

Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State

`/claude-tweaks:wrap-up` Phase 1 mints a standalone run dir when nothing resolves and stamps `run-state.json` with `{"status":"active","createdBy":"wrap-up-standalone"}` — no `sessionId`. #4138 made every exit after that mint close a created directory except the Review Console's "Stop and re-engage" halt (`wrap-up/review-console-interactive.md` "On stop"), which deliberately leaves it open for `/claude-tweaks:wrap-up resume`. But `resume` (`wrap-up/resume-halted-run.md`) only finds a run whose `run-state.json` has `status: interrupted`, and the SessionEnd hook (`plugin/bin/lib/hooks/session-end.js`) stamps `interrupted` only on a run attributed by ownership, never on a `fallback` guess. A created standalone wrap-up dir records no owning session, so it most likely stays `active` and `resume` can never find it. Unverified: probe the SessionEnd attribution for such a dir before building.

## Deliverables

Confirm the gap with a fixture: a created wrap-up standalone dir halted at Stop, then a session end, then `resume`. If confirmed, make the halt resumable — e.g. the "On stop" branch stamps the created directory so `resume` can find it (a sanctioned `hooks.js` writer, not a hand edit), or `resume` also accepts an `active` `createdBy: "wrap-up-standalone"` directory whose console was halted. Update `resume-halted-run.md` and the Stop branch to match.

## Acceptance Criteria

A created standalone wrap-up run halted at "Stop and re-engage" is found by `/claude-tweaks:wrap-up resume` in a later session, pinned by a test that fails before the fix. An inherited (pipeline) run's resume behavior is unchanged. `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

A standalone wrap-up paused at the Review Console can be resumed later with `/claude-tweaks:wrap-up resume`.

## Technical Approach

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/wrap-up/resume-halted-run.md` — modify
- `plugin/skills/wrap-up/review-console-interactive.md` — modify

Origin: /claude-tweaks:release v6.154.1 whole-branch review, delta 43c11df0e..5fb12cb2c (run 2026-10-21T194624-release-standalone, staged/review-37.md); reproduced by an executed probe in /bin/bash 3.2 and Homebrew bash 5

Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State

`plugin/bin/lib/hooks/git-command.js`'s `DATA_READER_WORDS` (~line 889: cat, tee, gh, read, node, python, python3, jq, wc) decides a heredoc body is data by the reader's command name. A function defined earlier in the same command shadows that name: `cat() { sh; }` then `cat <<'EOF'\necho hi > w\nEOF` runs the body as shell, while the scanner strips it and `fileWriteTargets` returns `[]`.

Probe: scanner targets `[]`, file `w` written by bash. Pre-existing — the allowlist predates #4149, which only extended stripping to unquoted bodies.

The same name-trust gap applies to an `alias` (only in interactive shells, so not reachable from `bash -c`) and to `node`/`python` already on the list, which execute stdin by design (the accepted opaque-program gap recorded in `_shared/policy-schema-coverage.md`).

## Deliverables

1. When the command text defines a shell function (`name() {`, `name () {`, `function name`) whose name is in `DATA_READER_WORDS`, treat every heredoc fed to that name in the same command as not-data: keep its body visible to the write scan.

2. State the admission rule for `DATA_READER_WORDS` in a comment beside the list, with a pointer to ADR 0027.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `fileWriteTargets("cat() { sh; }\ncat <<'EOF'\necho hi > w\nEOF\n", cwd)` resolves `w`.

- `fileWriteTargets("cat <<'EOF'\necho hi > w\nEOF\n", cwd)` still returns `[]` (no shadowing function).

- A test in `tests/hooks-gate-coverage.test.js` pins both and goes red when the fix is reverted.

- `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

The worktree-always write gate no longer treats a heredoc as data when the command redefines its reader (for example `cat() { sh; }`).

## Technical Approach

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/git-command.js` — detect a same-command function shadowing a data reader
- `tests/hooks-gate-coverage.test.js` — function-shadow cases

groups.body:
**Related:** #4245

Origin: /claude-tweaks:release v6.154.1 whole-branch review, delta 43c11df0e..5fb12cb2c (run 2026-10-21T194624-release-standalone, staged/review-36.md); reproduced by an executed probe in /bin/bash 3.2 and Homebrew bash 5

Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State

`plugin/bin/lib/hooks/git-command.js` (~line 1442, the heredoc keep/strip decision) keeps an unquoted heredoc body visible to the write scan only when the body matches `/\$\(|`/`. Bash removes backslash-newline from an unquoted heredoc body before expansion, so `$\` at the end of one line followed by `(echo hi > w)` on the next is a command substitution that runs and writes `w`. The literal text holds no `$(`, so the scanner strips the body as data and `fileWriteTargets` returns `[]`.

Probe: `cat <<EOF\n$\\\n(echo hi > w_cont)\nEOF\n`. Scanner targets: `[]`. File `w_cont` is written by both `/bin/bash` 3.2 and bash 5. A write into the main checkout passes the worktree-always gate this way.

Pre-existing. Before #4149 the scanner missed even a plain `$(…)` heredoc write; #4149 closed the plain case, not this one. #4245 (backslash-newline outside heredoc bodies) explicitly leaves heredoc body lines unchanged, so it does not cover this.

## Deliverables

1. Before testing an unquoted heredoc body for expansions, join backslash-newline pairs the way bash does for unquoted bodies (a quoted delimiter `<<'EOF'` leaves the body literal and stays stripped).

2. Apply the same joined text to the backtick test, so `` `\<newline>cmd` `` forms are caught too.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `fileWriteTargets('cat <<EOF\n$\\\n(echo hi > w)\nEOF\n', cwd)` resolves `w`.

- `fileWriteTargets("cat <<'EOF'\n$\\\n(echo hi > w)\nEOF\n", cwd)` still returns `[]` (quoted delimiter: bash writes nothing).

- A test in `tests/hooks-gate-coverage.test.js` pins both cases and goes red when the fix is reverted; the shell-scanner bash differential agrees with bash on both.

- `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

The worktree-always write gate now catches a command substitution split across lines with a backslash inside an unquoted heredoc.

## Technical Approach

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/git-command.js` — join backslash-newline in unquoted heredoc bodies before the keep test
- `tests/hooks-gate-coverage.test.js` — continuation-in-heredoc cases

Origin: #2767 class split — classification of windows-regression run 40169646104 (main 6a41ebe3a)

Defer-reason: genuinely-larger

**Related:** #2767, #2783, #1782

## Current State

`logWindowsLongpathsEvent` (`plugin/bin/lib/hooks/post-tool-use.js:367`) writes to `ctx.ownedRun.dir` whenever that field is set. The ad-hoc stamp in the same file (`stampAdHocRunDir`, line 289) first checks `ctxLib.isTrustedOwnedRun(ctx.ownedRun)`, because "a 'fallback' guess does not count (#2783)". The breadcrumb writer has no such check, so an EnterWorktree in a checkout that holds an unrelated run dir writes the `windows-longpaths` event into that unrelated run. `checkWindowsLongpaths` (line 373) runs only when `ctx.platform || process.platform` is `win32` (line 375). On Linux CI this path never runs in the end-to-end repro.

`tests/friction-adhoc-enterworktree-roundtrip.test.js:21` is #2783's own repro. It asserts that the run resolved at EnterWorktree is the `fallback` guess, which is the unrelated sibling run (line 31). It passes that run as `ctx.ownedRun` to `post.run` with no `platform` (lines 33-37). On Windows it fails at line 64 with `nothing may land in the unrelated sibling run`.

`logWorktreeStalenessEvent` (line 350) has the same unguarded shape.

1 test in 1 file fails on Windows (line numbers as of 988cc584d).

### Failing tests

- `tests/friction-adhoc-enterworktree-roundtrip.test.js:21` — #2783 repro: the harness refusal from an ad-hoc EnterWorktree session survives ExitWorktree remove

## Deliverables

- Route both breadcrumb writers, `logWindowsLongpathsEvent` and `logWorktreeStalenessEvent`, through one helper. The helper appends only when `ctxLib.isTrustedOwnedRun(ctx.ownedRun)` is true. A `fallback` guess gets nothing.
- Keep #1782's breadcrumb for a run that is actually owned. Any non-`fallback` attribution (`context.js:771`) still receives the `windows-longpaths` event.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. AC1: `node --test tests/friction-adhoc-enterworktree-roundtrip.test.js tests/hooks-post-tool-use-worktree-staleness.test.js` passes on Linux.
2. AC2: a Linux-runnable win32 repro through the existing `ctx.platform` seam. The roundtrip test's `post.run` call carries `platform: 'win32'`, so Linux CI covers the Windows path. It fails before the fix and passes after.
3. AC3: unit pins in `tests/hooks-post-tool-use-worktree-staleness.test.js` with `platform: 'win32'`. With a `fallback` `ownedRun`, no `events.jsonl` is created in that dir. With a `session` `ownedRun`, exactly one `windows-longpaths` event lands there.
4. AC4: go-red. Removing the trust check from the helper fails AC2 and AC3's fallback case.
5. AC5: a `windows-regression.yml` dispatch on the branch shows `tests/friction-adhoc-enterworktree-roundtrip.test.js` with 0 failures of this class and no newly failing file.

## Release Note

Windows: the `core.longpaths` breadcrumb no longer lands in an unrelated pipeline run's `events.jsonl` after an ad-hoc EnterWorktree.

## Gotchas

- ASSUMPTION — verify at build: the event that landed in the sibling run on the Windows run was `windows-longpaths`. The log shows only the assertion message. The inference is that `checkWindowsLongpaths` is the only win32-only writer on this path. AC2 confirms or refutes it on Linux before any fix.
- `stampAdHocRunDir` does not update `ctx.ownedRun`. Whether the freshly minted ad-hoc dir should receive the breadcrumb is a build-time decision. This record only requires that a fallback guess never does.

## Technical Approach

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/post-tool-use.js` — one trust-gated breadcrumb helper used by both writers
- `tests/friction-adhoc-enterworktree-roundtrip.test.js` — `platform: 'win32'` on the repro's `post.run` call
- `tests/hooks-post-tool-use-worktree-staleness.test.js` — fallback and session ownership pins

groups.body:
Origin: #2767 class split — classification of windows-regression run 40169646104 (main 6a41ebe3a)

Defer-reason: genuinely-larger

**Related:** #2767, #4146 (this record takes its G part), #4134 (owns the test-impact tracer half of class G, the NODE_OPTIONS `--require` splice, including #4254), #3517, #3599

## Current State

Shipped skill prose splices `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` into JavaScript source. The shell expands it inside `node -e "…"` strings and inside unquoted `node-eval-file.js` heredoc bodies, so it lands in a JS string literal. There, `\a`, `\_` and `\c` are eaten as escapes and `\u` is a SyntaxError. A Windows root such as `D:\a\claude-tweaks\…` therefore reaches `require` as `D:aclaude-tweaks…`. The failing evidence is `Cannot find module 'D:aclaude-tweaksclaude-tweaksplugin/bin/lib/issues/grant-maturation.js'`.

How far it reaches: `grep -rhoE "require\(['\"]\\$\{?CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT" plugin/skills` finds 244 occurrences across 61 files. There are also non-`require` literals: `const path = '${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/CHANGELOG.md'` (`plugin/skills/init/bootstrap/version-check.md:58`) and `fs.readFileSync('${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}…` (`plugin/skills/init/update-mode.md:64`). The failing tests run these sites:

- `plugin/skills/dispatch/grant-maturation-gate.md:32`, `:79`
- `plugin/skills/wrap-up/auto-merge-short-circuit.md:28`, `:56`, `:86`
- `plugin/skills/backlog/attention-mode.md:42`, `:58`, `:120`

Some snippets already pass values as data, for example `plugin/skills/wrap-up/auto-merge-short-circuit.md:192` and `plugin/skills/wrap-up/refused-proposals.md:16`, which read `process.argv[1]`. Five suites work around the splice by forward-slashing the root inside the test (`tests/dispatch-mcp-timestamp-alias.test.js:60-62` and four siblings), which hides the production shape.

`tests/comment-trust-conformance.test.js:483` also splices native temp paths for the `$ST_*` variables. Production prints those with `/` on win32 (`plugin/bin/session-tmp-resolve.js:26-27`, `formatPrintedPath`), so that half is test-only.

3 tests in 1 file fail on Windows (line numbers as of 988cc584d). The 18 failing `tests/test-impact-tracer.test.js` tests in the same class come from a different splice, NODE_OPTIONS `--require "<native path>"`. They are handed to #4134.

### Failing tests

- `tests/comment-trust-conformance.test.js:283` — grant maturation snippet in dispatch/grant-maturation-gate.md runs: a NONE pending-grant marker is skipped with a note, a MEMBER one counts
- `tests/comment-trust-conformance.test.js:283` — grant maturation snippet in wrap-up/auto-merge-short-circuit.md runs: a NONE pending-grant marker is skipped with a note, a MEMBER one counts
- `tests/comment-trust-conformance.test.js:483` — attention-mode.md merge script runs: a forged newer NONE proposal is skipped with a note, the MEMBER one is read

## Deliverables

- Remove every JS-literal splice of `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` from `plugin/skills/**`. Pass the root as an argument after the script and read it from `process.argv`: `require(require('path').join(process.argv[1], 'bin/lib/x.js'))`. A `node-eval-file.js` heredoc body reads it from its own argv. Paths stay native, and nothing respells the plugin root.
- Add a conformance suite that scans `plugin/skills/**/*.md` for `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` inside a quoted JS literal, in a `node -e` body or a `NODE_EVAL_EOF` heredoc. Give it a go-red self-test.
- `tests/comment-trust-conformance.test.js` passes the root to each snippet as argv. Its `$ST_*` stand-ins use the form `formatPrintedPath` prints.
- Drop the forward-slash workarounds in the five suites that carry them, so they run with a native root.
- Plan-review decision (Reading B): the `{plugin-root}` placeholder splices in `plugin/skills/harness-health/judge-procedure.md` (`require('{plugin-root}/bin/lib/session-tmp.js')` and `require('{plugin-root}/bin/lib/skill-audit/bloat.js')`, both inside `node -e`) are in scope and are rewritten the same way as the `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` sites.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. AC1: `node --test tests/comment-trust-conformance.test.js tests/node-eval-file-heredoc-syntax.test.js` and the new conformance suite pass on Linux. The full `npm test` also passes, because skill prose is pinned by many suites.
2. AC2: a Linux-runnable proof of the Windows shape. A temp symlink whose name holds backslashes (`x\a\_temp`, a legal POSIX file name) points at `plugin/`. With that path as the root, each snippet `tests/comment-trust-conformance.test.js` runs passes.
3. AC3: go-red for AC2. Running one snippet in its pre-change splice form with the same root fails with `Cannot find module`.
4. AC4: the conformance scan reports 0 splices, and its self-test flags a doctored `require('${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/x.js')`.
5. AC5: a `windows-regression.yml` dispatch on the branch shows `tests/comment-trust-conformance.test.js` with 0 failures of this class (its jq-CRLF failures belong to #3995) and no newly failing file.
- The conformance scan also fails on a `{plugin-root}` JS-literal splice under `plugin/skills/**`, not only on `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`.

## Release Note

Windows: skill steps that load plugin modules through `node -e` no longer fail with `Cannot find module` when the plugin is installed under a backslash path.

## Gotchas

- ASSUMPTION — verify at build: Claude Code on Windows exposes `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` to a skill's Bash commands as a native backslash path. If it already uses forward slashes, the prose change is still correct but has no user-visible effect, and the test fixes are needed either way.
- `node-eval-file.js` (lines 23-28) forbids any `$` in a heredoc body other than `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`. Once the root moves to argv, the delimiter can be quoted (`<<'NODE_EVAL_EOF'`). Check each body for other expansions before quoting it.
- Conformance suites extract these snippets by anchored fence text (`snippetBody` in `tests/comment-trust-conformance.test.js`, line 255). Run the full suite.
- 61 prose files make a large diff. Consider splitting it into sub-issues by skill directory, with the conformance suite landing last.

## Technical Approach

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/**/*.md` (61 files) — the root passed as argv instead of spliced into JS
- `tests/plugin-root-splice-conformance.test.js` — new scan plus go-red self-test
- `tests/comment-trust-conformance.test.js` — snippets run with a native or backslash-named root through argv
- `tests/dispatch-mcp-timestamp-alias.test.js`, `tests/dispatch-near-dup-pairs-script.test.js`, `tests/dispatch-named-target-exclusion-fixture.test.js`, `tests/dispatch-neighbour-in-flight-mcp.test.js`, `tests/release-run-dir-lifecycle-conformance.test.js` — forward-slash workarounds dropped

Origin: ledger resolve gate (run 2026-10-25T090732-record-4210, refs #4210; items 11, 14, 15, 16)

Defer-reason: genuinely-larger

## Current State

#4210 teaches the Bash gate parsers to track `"$( … )"` / `"${ … }"` / backtick nesting so a quoted `>` is never read as a redirect. Two separate walkers do it today: `advanceNesting` in `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/git-command.js` (the redirect scan) and the `subs` stack in `scanHeredocs` (heredoc stripping). Each re-derives shell quoting for its own purpose, and the heuristics still disagree with bash in four shapes, found by #4210's review and wrap-up:

- An unmatched closer inside `"$( … )"` (`case a)` patterns, a bare `}`) closes the nesting early and names a junk target: `echo "$(case $x in a) echo "p>q";; esac)"` resolves `/r/q;; esac)` (main resolved nothing). Fails closed (a false deny).
- An unquoted-delimiter heredoc inside `"$( … )"` whose body holds both `$(` and an apostrophe keeps its body visible, so the `'` leaves the nesting open and a later genuine redirect resolves nothing: `git commit -m "$(cat <<EOF\nDon't $(date)\nEOF\n)" && echo y > o.js`. Fails open.
- An unquoted `echo $(cmd x>y)` resolves the target `y)` (the group closer stays in the name). Pre-existing on main.

## Deliverables

- [ ] Replace the two nesting walkers with one shared word-lexer that understands `$( … )` (including `case` patterns and heredoc bodies), `${ … }`, backticks, and quote state, and have both the redirect scan and `stripHeredocBodies` read it.
- [ ] Make the four shapes above resolve as bash does, keeping the never-fabricate posture: ambiguity resolves to no target.
- [ ] Pin each shape in `tests/hooks-gate-coverage.test.js` and the prefilter differential corpus in `tests/hooks-bash-prefilter.test.js`, and run the old and new parsers over a shared command corpus, accounting for every changed result.

## Acceptance Criteria

`fileWriteTargets('echo "$(case $x in a) echo "p>q";; esac)"', cwd)` resolves nothing, and `fileWriteTargets("git commit -m \"$(cat <<EOF\nDon't $(date)\nEOF\n)\" && echo y > o.js", cwd)` resolves `o.js`.
`fileWriteTargets('echo $(cmd x>y)', cwd)` resolves `y`, not `y)`.
`npm test` and `npm run test:perf` pass, and the `hooks-prefilter` perf budget holds.

## Release Note

The worktree-always gate reads nested command substitutions the way bash does, so fewer harmless commands are denied and no write slips past it.

## Technical Approach

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/git-command.js` — one shared nesting lexer for advanceNesting and scanHeredocs
- `tests/hooks-gate-coverage.test.js` — pin the four shapes
- `tests/hooks-bash-prefilter.test.js` — add the shapes to the differential corpus

Origin: ledger resolve gate (run 2026-10-24T200414-record-4015, refs #4015)

Defer-reason: genuinely-larger

## Current State

`plugin/bin/lib/hooks/git-command.js`'s `redirectWriteTargets` reads one target per operator token. A chained redirect such as `echo a>b>c` (glued, from #4015) or `2>/dev/null>x` (start-anchored, from #3080) is one token, so the scan resolves the single joined name `b>c`. Bash writes both `b` and `c`.

The gate verdict for the joined name is not always the verdict for the real targets: it depends on the mix of absolute and relative parts, so the claim that the verdict is unchanged is not universally true. #4015's final whole-branch review asked for a follow-up record with corrected wording.

Telling which `>` inside a token is bare needs the same per-span quote record that the quoted-word glued redirect follow-up adds to `tokenize` (a quoted `>` such as `a>"b>c"` is data), so this lands after or with that change.

## Deliverables

- [ ] Split the target of a bare (unquoted) token at each further `>`, `>>` or `>|` and resolve every piece, for the glued and the start-anchored forms.
- [ ] Keep a quoted `>` in the target data: `echo a>"b>c"` resolves the one file `b>c`.
- [ ] Correct the wording in `plugin/skills/_shared/policy-schema-coverage.md` and `docs/journeys/write-a-glued-redirect-from-the-main-checkout-4015.md` that lists chained redirects as a known gap.

Surface: infra

**Related:** #4202, #4180, #4253, #3193, #3977, #3990, #4217, #4285, #4289

Origin: #4202 whole-branch review (Minor 4)

Defer-reason: needs-human-decision

## Current State

- `pruneResidueFailures` (`plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/cache.js:393-415`) deletes a `residueFailures` entry whose path is gone from disk (`delete failures[key]`, `:403`) *before* its best-effort resolve. It keeps that deletion whatever the resolve returns. A failed resolve is only reported, through the returned `failures` list (`:409-411`).
- Since #4202, an archive success resolves an escalated `structurally-stuck` entry through `clearResidue` (`:300`), which keeps the entry when that resolve fails (`:315`; pinned by `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/cache.test.js:432`, "#2724 clearResidue: an escalated entry whose resolve returns resolution-failed is kept for the next pass"). The same pass's prune then retries exactly once and drops the entry regardless. So a resolve that fails twice in one pass (a `gh` outage) leaves the path orphaned on the consolidated record.
- This drop-on-failure posture is deliberate. #1892 Deliverable 3 documents it ("a resolution failure still drops the cache entry"), and two tests pin it: `cache.test.js:352` ("…triggers exactly one resolve call… and is still dropped") and `:371` ("a resolve failure (gh absent / network) still drops the cache entry, never throws").
- #4202's convergence only drops an orphan on a later edit of the record. When the orphan was the last listed path, the record stays open until an unrelated stuck dir is escalated or resolved.
- `recordResidueError` (`:264`) already records the last failed op and reason on a kept entry (#4180), as `lastResidueError`. The cache schema has no retry counter today.

## Deliverables

1. Make `pruneResidueFailures` keep an escalated entry whose resolve did not land, the way `clearResidue` already does, so the next pass retries it. "Did not land" means a status outside `RESIDUE_RESOLVED_STATUSES` (`:288`) or a throw.
2. Bound the gh-absent posture so a machine with no `gh` does not retry forever. Count failed prune retries on the entry and drop it after a fixed bound, never reverting to drop-on-first-failure. Document the bound beside the existing #1892 comment (`cache.test.js:325`) and in the function's header.
3. Update the two tests that pin the old posture (`cache.test.js:352`, `:371`) to the new contract, and keep the non-escalated drop test (`:328`) unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/cache.test.js` test: an escalated entry whose path is gone and whose injected resolve returns `resolution-failed` survives `pruneResidueFailures`. It fails when the change is reverted.
- [ ] A test pins the bound: after the configured number of failed prune retries the entry is dropped, and the returned `failures` list still reports each failed resolve.
- [ ] A non-escalated entry whose path is gone is still dropped without a resolve call (the existing `:328` test passes unchanged).
- [ ] `npm test` is green.

## Release Note

Reconcile no longer forgets a stuck run directory's escalation when GitHub is briefly unreachable.

## Technical Approach

Move the `delete failures[key]` for escalated entries to after the resolve, and delete only on a resolved status or once the retry bound is reached. Store the count on the entry itself (for example `pruneRetries`), next to the `lastResidueError` field #4180 added (`cache.js:65`). That way the bound survives across passes and needs no new cache key. Non-escalated entries keep today's immediate drop, since they never had a GitHub-side record to resolve.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/cache.js` — `pruneResidueFailures` keep-on-failure plus retry bound; entry schema comment (`:65`)
- `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/cache.test.js` — new keep and bound tests; rewrite the `:352` and `:371` pins

## Gotchas

- This reverses a documented decision (#1892 Deliverable 3). The record was filed with `Defer-reason: needs-human-decision` for that reason, and the reversal is the subject of this record, not a side effect. A reviewer should confirm the chosen bound before merge. The bound's value is the one open choice, and it is left to the plan to propose.
- `pruneResidueFailures` is reason-agnostic by design (`cache.test.js:325-327`, shared with #1811's structurally-stuck prune). The keep-on-failure rule applies to every escalated entry, not only `structurally-stuck`.
- #4253 (open, `ready`) retries a failed residue *escalation* in the same `cache.js`, and its Key Files overlap this record. Its retry bound and this one should share one counter shape and one bound constant, never two parallel conventions. Whichever lands second adopts the first one.
- Callers read the returned `{ failures }` list for reporting. Keep reporting each failed resolve even when the entry is kept, so a gh outage stays visible in the reconcile output.

## Original request

reconcile: pruneResidueFailures drops an escalated entry whose retry resolve failed, orphaning its path

**Related:** #4202, #4180

Origin: #4202 whole-branch review (Minor 4)

Defer-reason: needs-human-decision

## Current State

- `pruneResidueFailures` (`plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/cache.js` ~286) deletes a `residueFailures` entry whose path is gone from disk *before* its best-effort resolve, and keeps the deletion whatever that resolve returns.
- Since #4202, an archive success resolves an escalated `structurally-stuck` entry through `clearResidue`, which keeps the entry when that resolve fails. The same pass's prune then retries exactly once and drops the entry regardless, so a resolve that fails twice in one pass (a `gh` outage) leaves the path orphaned on the consolidated record.
- This drop-on-failure posture is deliberate: #1892 Deliverable 3 documents it ("a resolution failure still drops the cache entry"), and `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/cache.test.js` pins it. Keeping the entry instead, and choosing a retry bound for a machine with no `gh`, reverses that decision, so it needs a human call.
- #4202's convergence only drops an orphan on a later edit of the record. When the orphan was the last listed path, the record stays open until an unrelated stuck dir is escalated or resolved.

## Deliverables

1. Make `pruneResidueFailures` keep an escalated entry whose resolve did not land (a status outside `RESIDUE_RESOLVED_STATUSES`, or a throw), the way `clearResidue` already does, so the next pass retries it.
2. Decide and document the gh-absent posture: a machine with no `gh` would otherwise retry forever. Bound it (for example, drop after N failed prune retries, recording the count on the entry) rather than reverting to drop-on-first-failure.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/cache.test.js` test: an escalated entry whose path is gone and whose injected resolve returns `resolution-failed` survives `pruneResidueFailures`; it fails when the change is reverted.
- [ ] A test pins the bound: after the configured number of failed prune retries the entry is dropped.
- [ ] `npm test` is green.

Reconcile no longer forgets a stuck run directory's escalation when GitHub is briefly unreachable.

Surface: infra

**Related:** #3813, #4125, #4162

Origin: #3950 final whole-branch review, finding I2 (PR #3992)
Defer-reason: genuinely-larger

## Current State

`/claude-tweaks:tidy`'s console backfill mode (`plugin/skills/tidy/console-backfill.md`, CLI `plugin/bin/console-backfill.js`) settles Review Console residue left in archived runs: it files records, posts digest lines, and rewrites each `console.json`. Its filing and digest steps go through GitHub Issues only (`gh issue create`, `gh issue comment` on the digest issue), so Step 3's backend gate stops any project whose `work-backend` is not `github-issues` with:

`HELD — console backfill needs work-backend: github-issues; local-files support is tracked as the backlog record "Console backfill: settle Review Console residue under work-backend: local-files"`

A `work-backend: local-files` project therefore keeps every unreviewed console item forever, and its session-start residue notice never clears except by a blanket `console-residue.js --ack-all`.

## Deliverables

- Console backfill runs under `work-backend: local-files`: filings become local record files through the same writer `/claude-tweaks:capture` uses under that backend, and digest lines append to the local digest the materiality floor names for that backend (`_shared/materiality-floor.md`).
- Filing dedup (claim fingerprint and `consolebackfill-item` marker) and digest dedup read the local records and local digest, so the crash-resume guarantees hold as they do on GitHub.
- Step 3's backend gate passes `local-files`; the HELD line is removed or narrowed to backends that remain unsupported, and its pin in `tests/tidy-console-backfill-conformance.test.js` is updated.

## Acceptance Criteria

- On a `local-files` fixture project with one archived run holding a confirmed finding, a digest-bound finding and a dismissal, a backfill pass leaves one local record, one local digest line, and a `console.json` whose items all carry a `ref`.
- A second pass over the same fixture writes nothing.
- A pass interrupted after the record write and resumed after a claim-text change reuses that record rather than writing a second one.

## Release Note

Console backfill now settles Review Console residue in projects that keep work records as local files.

## Technical Approach

The CLI already plans from data the procedure hands it, so most of the change belongs in the procedure. `console-backfill.js dispose` takes `--existing` (today a `gh issue list --state all --json number,title,body` array) and `--digest-comments` (the digest issue's comment objects) (`plugin/bin/console-backfill.js:10-22`). Under `local-files`, the procedure builds `--existing` from `queryRecords` (`bin/lib/issues/local-store.js`) mapped to the same `{number,title,body}` shape, and passes the current `specs/digest.md` body as the digest input. `_shared/materiality-floor.md:70` already names that body a trusted single-writer string. Filing uses `createRecord`, the writer `/claude-tweaks:capture` uses under `local-files` (`plugin/skills/capture/SKILL.md:306-310`), and never `allocateId` + `writeRecord`. Digest lines append to `specs/digest.md` (`_shared/materiality-floor.md:158`).

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/tidy/console-backfill.md` — backend gate and filing/digest steps
- `plugin/bin/lib/console/backfill-dispose.js` — filing and digest planning
- `plugin/bin/console-backfill.js` — `dispose` inputs (`--existing`, `--digest-comments`) for the local-files shapes
- `tests/tidy-console-backfill-conformance.test.js` — HELD-line pin (`:55`)
- `tests/bin-lib/console/backfill-dispose.test.js` — local-files planning cases

## Gotchas

- Under `local-files`, a record file and `specs/digest.md` are tracked files. Each landed write needs a commit, which the GitHub path never needs, so the procedure must run in a worktree and commit per write. Otherwise a crash leaves an uncommitted record that the next pass's `queryRecords` still sees. That is fine for dedup, but it must be committed before `console.json` cites it.
- A local record's ref is its id, not `#N` under a GitHub repo. Check that `apply`'s `ref` field and the residue reader (`lib/console/residue.js`) accept the local ref form before the console item is marked settled.
- The digest dedup input differs by backend: comment objects with author association on GitHub, a trusted file body on local-files (`_shared/materiality-floor.md:63-70`). `heldDigestComment` in `backfill-dispose.js` must take the local form without treating it as an untrusted comment.
- The HELD line is pinned verbatim in `tests/tidy-console-backfill-conformance.test.js:55` and also names this record by title. Update both when narrowing the gate.

Surface: infra

**Related:** #3942, #4038, #4163

Origin: #3950 final fix-wave re-review (PR #3992)
Defer-reason: genuinely-larger

## Current State

`plugin/bin/lib/console/backfill-dispose.js`'s filing dedup survives a claim-heuristic change by matching each finding's `consolebackfill-{hash(itemId)}` item marker (#3950 fix wave, I1.5). One case still files a twin:

1. In one backfill pass, items A and B share a claim fingerprint. A is filed; B is planned as `reuse sameAs A`, so the created record carries only A's item marker.
2. The session crashes after the record is created and before `apply` settles B.
3. A plugin upgrade changes the claim cleaning before the next pass, so B's claim fingerprint moves.
4. The next pass finds A by its marker, but B matches neither its claim fingerprint nor its own marker, and is filed again.

Even when A's and B's new claims still match each other, the "matched an existing record" branch never records the fingerprint in the batch's filed map, so B does not fall back to `sameAs A` either. The digest path has the same shape: B's line was never posted, so B posts a second line under its new fingerprint.

Exposure is narrow — it needs a crash in that window, an upgrade between passes, and a same-claim pair — and the damage is one recoverable duplicate record or digest line.

## Deliverables

- A filing planned for item A also carries the item marker of every same-pass item planned `sameAs A`, so each of them is found by its own marker on the next pass.
- The "matched an existing record" branch records `fingerprint → record number` in the batch's filed map, so a later same-fingerprint item in the pass reuses it.
- The same treatment for digest lines: a digest duplicate planned `sameAs` a same-pass line is found by its own marker on the next pass.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A test plans A and B with one claim fingerprint, simulates a crash after A's record is created, changes B's claim text, and re-plans: B reuses A's record and nothing is filed. The test fails against the code before the fix.
- A test where an existing record matches A and B shares A's fingerprint: B is `sameAs` that record, not a new filing.
- The digest equivalent of the first test: no second digest line for B.

## Release Note

Console backfill no longer files a duplicate record when a crash and a plugin upgrade both land between two passes over a same-claim pair.

## Technical Approach

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/console/backfill-dispose.js` — filing and digest planning
- `tests/bin-lib/console/backfill-dispose.test.js` — the three tests above

## Gotchas

- Premise probed at HEAD: the matched-record branch (`if (matched !== null)`, `plugin/bin/lib/console/backfill-dispose.js:441-443`) pushes `reuse` without touching `batchFiled`, and only the new-filing branch calls `batchFiled.set(fp, d.itemId)` (`:447`). Confirmed.
- `batchFiled` maps a fingerprint to an **item id**, which a later `sameAs` resolves once that item's record exists. A matched existing record already has a number, so a later same-fingerprint item should reuse that number directly (`{ number: matched }`). Recording the number in the same map would need a value-shape distinction that its other readers do not expect.
- The item marker is `<!-- consolebackfill-item: {hash} -->` (`itemMarkerOf`, `:99-100`). Carrying several of them on one filed body must keep `filedRecordOf`'s marker lookup matching each marker independently.

Surface: infra

**Related:** #4038, #3295, #3758, #3835, #3963, #3978, #4102, #4252, #4269, #4345

## Current State

`plugin/skills/design-wrapper/modes/review.md` Step 5.5 ("Stage decisions findings") tells the agent to "write one file to `{run-dir}/staged/`" for each `target: "decisions"` finding (`review.md:465`), and to "Log one line per file written to `decisions.md`" (`review.md:496`). It names neither sanctioned writer. When `/claude-tweaks:review` Step 6.5 dispatches this mode from a worktree session, the anchored run dir is in the main checkout, so the worktree-isolation guard refuses both direct writes. The mode's recovery rule ("If a stage write fails, surface a one-time skip and continue", `review.md:499`) then drops the finding from the Review Console. In the observed run, the two findings reached the console only because the controller copied them in by hand.

The same mode carries two more direct `decisions.md` appends that hit the same guard:

- Step 3.8(a): "Log one line per `../../_shared/auto-decision-log.md`: `AUTO {time} — review Step 3.8: design-critique resolved to …`" (`review.md:173-174`).
- `plugin/skills/design-wrapper/modes/review-seed-capture.md:56`: "Log one `AUTO` entry to `{run-dir}/decisions.md`" for a seed write.

No file under `plugin/skills/design-wrapper/` mentions `bin/log-decision.js` or `bin/stage-item.js`. By contrast, the controller-side polish path (`plugin/skills/flow/polish-execution.md`) already stages through `stage-item.js`.

The sanctioned writers exist: `plugin/bin/stage-item.js` (`--run <run-dir> --id <kind>-<n> --file <path> [--allocate]`) and `plugin/bin/log-decision.js` (`--run <run-dir> --status … --text … [--section …]`).

**Premise correction.** The filed request says `--allocate` "also covers this mode's 'look for an existing file before allocating' rule." It does not. `plugin/bin/lib/stage-item/write.js:105-139` shows that `--allocate` *reallocates* a colliding id to the next free `{kind}-{n}`. It never dedupes by content. Step 5.5's dedupe rule ("identical `Provider:` + `File:` + `Message:` … overwrite it in place rather than allocating a new number", `review.md:477-480`) still needs its own lookup. A plain `--allocate` on every write would duplicate a finding on every re-review after polish's re-verify cycle.

## Deliverables

1. Step 5.5 stages each `decisions` finding through `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/stage-item.js" --run "$PIPELINE_RUN_DIR"`, writing the file body to a scratch path first:
   - The absence-nudge (`provider: wrapper`) uses the fixed id `design-decision-nudge`, without `--allocate`, so it keeps today's overwrite-in-place semantics.
   - Other findings first run the existing content-dedupe lookup, which is a read of `{run-dir}/staged/design-decision-*.md`. On a match, write with that file's id and no `--allocate` (a plain overwrite). Without a match, write `--id design-decision-1 --allocate`.
2. Step 5.5's STAGED line goes through `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/log-decision.js" --run "$PIPELINE_RUN_DIR" --status STAGED --section "/review" --step "review Step 5.5" --text "…"`. The text keeps today's wording and names the path the CLI actually wrote, which is the reallocated id when `--allocate` renamed it.
3. Step 3.8(a)'s AUTO lever line and `review-seed-capture.md`'s AUTO seed-write line both go through `bin/log-decision.js` the same way.
4. The recovery rule stays: a non-zero exit from either CLI is a one-time skip. `decisions_staged` counts only files that `stage-item.js` reported written.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `review.md` Step 5.5 names `bin/stage-item.js` for every staged-file write and `bin/log-decision.js` for every `decisions.md` line. No instruction in Step 5.5 tells the agent to write under `{run-dir}/` directly.
2. Step 5.5 keeps the content-dedupe rule. It calls `--allocate` only on the no-match branch and never on the nudge or a dedupe match.
3. `review.md` Step 3.8(a) and `review-seed-capture.md`'s seed-write logging name `bin/log-decision.js`.
4. A conformance test asserts AC 1-3 against the live prose of the two files. Reverting either file's edit turns the test red.
5. `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

Design review findings are now recorded reliably when the review runs inside an isolated worktree, without being copied over by hand.

## Technical Approach

This change is prose only, in the two design-wrapper mode files, plus one conformance test. The `$PIPELINE_RUN_DIR` the mode already receives is the anchored main-checkout run dir. Both CLIs anchor it themselves (the gh-api-module-pattern CLI wrapper contract), which is why the guard admits them where a direct `Write` is refused. Match the invocation shape `plugin/skills/flow/polish-execution.md` already uses for its own `stage-item.js` call.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/design-wrapper/modes/review.md` — Step 5.5 staging and logging; Step 3.8(a) lever log line
- `plugin/skills/design-wrapper/modes/review-seed-capture.md` — seed-write AUTO log line
- `plugin/skills/flow/polish-execution.md` — reference only: the existing `stage-item.js` call shape to mirror
- `tests/design-wrapper-review-stage-writers.test.js` — new conformance test for AC 4

## Gotchas

- `--allocate` is collision-avoidance, not dedupe (see Current State). Keep the dedupe lookup ahead of the write.
- `design-decision-nudge` is not a `{kind}-{n}` id. `stage-item.js` refuses `--allocate` on it (exit 2, `plugin/bin/stage-item.js:179`), so the nudge must never pass the flag.
- The score-history append (`.claude-tweaks/design/score-history.jsonl`, `review.md:412`) and the audit cache (`docs/plans/…-audit.json`, Step 5) write into the worktree, not the anchored run dir. They are outside this record's scope.
- `tests/release-run-dir-lifecycle-conformance.test.js` pins `design-decision-1.md` as a roster prefix. Keep the `design-decision-` filename prefix unchanged.
- Related, not duplicated: the `$(...)` snippet shape in `plugin/skills/review/review-effort-derivation.md` is tracked by #3822 and #3737.

## Original request

design-wrapper review: staged design-decision files and their decisions.md lines bypass stage-item.js and log-decision.js

**Related:** #4038

**Summary:** design-wrapper's `review` mode writes `staged/design-decision-{n}.md` and its `decisions.md` STAGED line directly, so when it runs as a dispatched agent inside a worktree-isolated session the harness refuses both writes, and the finding is lost unless the controller notices and copies it by hand.

**Kind:** Gap

**Affected component:** `skills/design-wrapper/modes/review.md` (Step 5.5, "Filename and idempotency" and the "Log one line per file written to `decisions.md`" instruction)

**Use case:**
In a `worktree-always` project, `/claude-tweaks:review` Step 6.5 dispatched design-wrapper `review` from a worktree session. The anchored run dir lives in the main checkout, so the worktree-isolation guard refused the agent's direct writes to `staged/design-decision-*.md` and to `decisions.md`. The agent reported "stage write failed" and, per the mode's own recovery rule, surfaced a skip, so the two findings reached the Review Console only because the controller copied them in by hand. The plugin already ships the sanctioned writers for this boundary: `bin/stage-item.js` (with `--allocate` for the per-invocation `{n}` counter, which also covers this mode's "look for an existing file before allocating" rule) and `bin/log-decision.js`. This mode's instructions name neither.

**Suggested change:**
1. Point Step 5.5's staging at `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/stage-item.js" --run "$PIPELINE_RUN_DIR" --id design-decision-{n} --file <scratch> --allocate`, and the STAGED line at `bin/log-decision.js`.
2. Sweep other staging sites that a dispatched agent may execute for the same direct-write pattern.

Related, not duplicated here: the `$(...)` snippet shape in `skills/review/review-effort-derivation.md` (`CTX_DIR=$(node … mint --print-dir …)`) is refused by the same guard; that half is tracked by #3822 and #3737.

**Definition:** Clear

**Plugin version:** 6.145.0

Surface: infra

**Related:** #3823, #3953, #3982, #3983, #3993

## Current State

The post-merge Windows check on commit 6c660b23c (merged PR #3916, run 40029571772) reported `tests/bin-lib/issues/comment-trust.test.js` newly failing. The failing test is "untrustedJqNote prints the same text as untrustedSkipNote, including a deleted (null) author and a missing association" (line 66). Its actual output ends every line with `\r\n`, where the expected value is `\n`-joined.

Root cause, reproduced on macOS against `main` at d02483933: native `jq` on Windows writes stdout in text mode, so every output newline becomes CRLF. The tests compare `spawnSync('jq', …).stdout` byte-for-byte against `\n`-joined text. Running the files with a `jq` shim on `PATH` that converts output `\n` to `\r\n` reproduces exactly four failures, and a CRLF file-read simulation adds none. This is not the `readText` CRLF-read class:

- `tests/bin-lib/issues/comment-trust.test.js` (8 tests: 6 pass, 2 fail):
  - "untrustedJqNote prints the same text…" (jq call at line 80)
  - "AC1.1: trustedJqSelect keeps a trusted comment on both transports (real jq)" (jq call at line 119; `split('\n')` leaves a trailing `\r` on each kept value)
- `tests/comment-trust-conformance.test.js` (37 tests: 35 pass, 2 fail):
  - "AC5.2: grant-lane-decision.md's jq lines run…"
  - "AC5.2: shaping-mode-stamping.md's jq lines run…"
  - Both go through the `runJq` helper's jq call at line 449.

`tests/comment-trust-conformance.test.js` was never filed. The latest Windows run's `verify-report` artifact (run 40030935846, head d02483933) lists both files in `baselineAdjudicated.failingFiles`. The conformance file has been red since it was introduced, so the per-push baseline diff never reports it as newly failing. These three `spawnSync('jq', …)` calls are the only non-probe jq invocations under `tests/`. Shipped plugin code is unaffected: `comment-trust.js` only builds the filter strings.

## Deliverables

1. Normalize jq's stdout to `\n` line endings at each of the three call sites (`tests/bin-lib/issues/comment-trust.test.js` lines 80 and 119, `tests/comment-trust-conformance.test.js` line 449) before any assertion reads it. Do this through one shared test helper rather than three hand-written replacements.
2. Fix both test files in this record, since they share the root cause.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. No assertion in either file reads raw `jq` stdout. Every one of the three non-probe `spawnSync('jq', …)` results is EOL-normalized first.
2. With a CRLF-emitting `jq` shim first on `PATH` (a wrapper that pipes real `jq` output through `perl -pe 's/\n/\r\n/'`), both files pass every test. Before the fix this reports 2 failures in each file.
3. Both files are green on Linux/macOS with the real `jq`. The `jq not found` skip path is unchanged.
4. The next post-merge `windows-regression.yml` run's `verify-report` artifact lists neither file in `baselineAdjudicated.failingFiles`.

## Release Note

Fix Windows-only failures in the comment-trust jq tests caused by native jq's CRLF output.

## Technical Approach

Add a small `runJq(args, input)` helper next to `readText` under `tests/helpers/`. It wraps `spawnSync('jq', args, { input, encoding: 'utf8' })` and returns the result with `stdout` normalized via `.replace(/\r\n/g, '\n')`. Route the three call sites through it, keeping each `status`/`stderr` assertion as-is. Normalizing at the read mirrors the house rule for the CRLF-read class (#3776, #3953): fix the input once instead of loosening every assertion.

### Key Files

- `tests/bin-lib/issues/comment-trust.test.js` — two jq calls routed through the helper
- `tests/comment-trust-conformance.test.js` — `runJq`'s jq call routed through the helper
- `tests/helpers/` — new shared jq-run helper (or extend an existing helper module)

## Gotchas

- Do not pass `jq --binary` / `-b` instead. That flag is documented for native Windows builds, and its behavior on the Linux/macOS jq versions CI and maintainers run is not established here. Normalizing in the test is platform-independent.
- The `--version` probes need no change: they only check `status`.
- CI runs on ubuntu only. AC2's shim is the pre-merge stand-in, and only the post-merge `windows-regression.yml` run proves the fix on Windows.

## Original request

Windows regression: 1 test file(s) newly failing after 6c660b23c

The post-merge Windows check failed on commit 6c660b23cb7b054f4908afabd7a30949e220e57c (compared against 2b943d781).

**Merged PR:** #3916 (https://github.com/thn-inc/claude-tweaks/pull/3916)

**Run:** https://github.com/thn-inc/claude-tweaks/actions/runs/40029571772

### Newly failing test files
- `tests/bin-lib/issues/comment-trust.test.js`

### Failure excerpts

#### `tests/bin-lib/issues/comment-trust.test.js`

```
not ok 3668 - untrustedJqNote prints the same text as untrustedSkipNote, including a deleted (null) author and a missing association
  ---
  duration_ms: 1095.4188
  type: 'test'
  location: 'D:\\a\\claude-tweaks\\claude-tweaks\\tests\\bin-lib\\issues\\comment-trust.test.js:66:1'
  failureType: 'testCodeFailure'
  error: |-
    Expected values to be strictly equal:
    + actual - expected
    
    + 'skipped marker comment https://x/c1 by eve (NONE) — not an owner, member, or collaborator\r\n' +
    +   'skipped marker comment https://x/c2 by unknown (NONE) — not an owner, member, or collaborator\r\n' +
```

Origin: reflect full from #3947

Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State

A skill step that dispatches agents or calls CLIs is specified in prose, and nothing at spec, plan or authoring time asks what happens when each of those calls fails.

In #3947 (Step 3.7, `plugin/skills/review/step3-tiebreak.md`), the SDD final review needed 1 Critical and 6 Important fixes, and the later 4-lens review found 23 more findings. Most of them were the same kind of gap: what the reviewer does when a dispatch fails or returns non-DONE, when `write-findings` exits 2, when `resolve-tiebreak` crashes, or when `log-decision.js` fails. Each was added after the fact, across fix commits a2d09600d, a645f740b, cc098dd27 and 494bb6045.

`docs/skill-authoring.md` and `plugin/skills/build/plan-authoring-checks.md` have no rule or check that asks for a failure path per external call.

## Deliverables

- `docs/skill-authoring.md` gains a rule: a step whose prose dispatches an agent or runs a CLI states, for each such call, its next move on failure (retry once / fallback rung / surface and stop) and the log line it writes.
- `plugin/skills/build/plan-authoring-checks.md` gains a check: a plan task that adds or changes such a step carries a failure-path table (call → failure mode → next move → log line) before its prose is written.
- A conformance test pins both texts.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `docs/skill-authoring.md` contains the failure-path rule and names the three next-move kinds.
2. `plan-authoring-checks.md` contains the failure-path table check and its trigger (a task touching a step that dispatches an agent or runs a CLI).
3. A test asserts both, and it was shown to go red without each text.

## Release Note

Skill steps that dispatch agents or run tools now have to say up front what happens when each call fails, so those gaps are found while planning instead of in review.

## Technical Approach

### Key Files

- `docs/skill-authoring.md` — add the failure-path rule
- `plugin/skills/build/plan-authoring-checks.md` — add the failure-path table check
