groups.body:
Surface: infra

**Related:** #2724 (auto-filed structurally-stuck tracker, kept), #3898 (release runs are owned there)

## Overview

Run directories pile up because nothing closes a run whose session died. Measured 2026-10-22: 78 empty `-adhoc-standalone` directories (0 staged items and 0 decision lines in every one), and 27 stale formal runs (20 open PRs, 6 closed-unmerged, 1 merged). A session that crashes never fires SessionEnd, so its run stays `active` forever. The SessionStart "unfinished runs" banner shows 3 only because `MAX_REPORTED = 3` caps it with no overflow line, and it has no liveness filter: it listed three runs that sibling sessions were probably still driving.

This record is the report-only half of the fix. It adds a pure disposition function (run shape by liveness verdict gives close, leave, or orphan, with a reason), runs it inside reconcile in report-only mode so reconcile says what it would close and closes nothing, narrows the SessionStart banner to dead-and-orphaned runs with an overflow line, and makes a session archive its own ad hoc run at SessionEnd. Closing for real is a later record that must ship in a release after this one, so every consumer project gets a dry run on its own pile first.

The asymmetry the maintainer agreed on governs every rule here: settle findings aggressively, close runs conservatively. Closing a run a live sibling session is still driving ends that run's enforcement and event logging invisibly. A run left open by mistake costs one more banner line.

**Complexity:** Medium
**Estimated tasks:** 8

## Non-Goals

- Reconcile closes nothing in this record. No `run-state.json` is flipped to `clean` by the new rows, no staged item is dropped, no directory is archived by them. Turning that on, and `close-run --abandon`, are #3978.
- Reconcile gains no GitHub write and no skill-file write, and never carries out a staged item's outcome. It never deletes a branch, removes a worktree, or changes claim labels.
- No filing of backlog records per orphaned run, and no listing of live sibling runs "for information"; both relocate the noise.
- No change to the existing merged, `orphaned-mint`, `adhoc-superseded`, and `abandoned-interrupted` archive paths beyond the `live` skip; replacing `abandoned-interrupted`'s recency test is #3979.
- Release runs (`-release-standalone`) closing at their own end is #3898's scope; this record only covers dead ones through the standalone row.
- Not the auto-filed structurally-stuck tracker (#2724), which stays as it is.

## Prerequisites

| Spec | Title | Status |
|------|-------|--------|
| #3973 | Add a run-liveness verdict module and an owner block in run-state.json | must merge first: this record consumes `runLiveness` |
| #3845 | A nested `claude -p` inside a pipeline session marks the parent's run interrupted at its SessionEnd | in progress; it also edits `session-end.js` and writes a false `interrupted` this record must tolerate |

## Current State

- `classifyRunDir(ctx, now)` in `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js` (line 1602) walks `CLASSIFY_ORDER = ['orphaned-mint', 'abandoned-interrupted', 'adhoc-superseded', 'merged', 'structurally-stuck']`. `adhoc-superseded` requires an ad hoc mint whose worktree is gone and a directory idle for `ADHOC_SUPERSEDED_TTL_MS` (30 days). `abandoned-interrupted` requires `status: interrupted` and no owner-attributed event within `STALE_INTERRUPTED_TTL_MS` (24 hours); `orphaned-mint` requires a directory with no `config.yml` idle for `ORPHAN_MINT_TTL_MS` (24 hours).
- `collectStaleRuns(cwd, { cache, exclude, pluginRoot })` in `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/session-residue.js` (line 56) walks `iterRunDirsWithState`, skips ad hoc directories (`isAdHocRunDir`), and stops at `MAX_REPORTED = 3` (line 36) with no overflow line. Its sibling `CONSOLE_OVERFLOW_LINE` (line 201) is the existing overflow pattern: `- … more run(s) may have unreviewed console items (newest 3 shown).`
- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/session-start.js` renders the banner; line 148 carries the instruction text "Say with it that only the session owning a run should close it: a listed run may be live in a sibling session right now, ...", the warning this record drops.
- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/session-end.js` stamps `{ status: 'interrupted', lastEvent: 'session-end' }` onto the session's own non-`fallback` run, then appends a `session-end` event.
- Staged items live in the run's `staged/` (and `spec-*/staged/`); `listStagedItems` and `hasStagedItems` are in `archive-merged.js` (lines 443 and 461). Kinds are classified by `classifyStagedItem(filename, text, siblingText)` in `plugin/bin/lib/console/resolve.js` (line 179); review findings are the `review-unconfirmed-` and `review-contested-`/`review-debate-` prefixes (`SECTION_MAP`, line 47).
- Reconcile writes its results to `.claude-tweaks/reconcile-cache.json` (`plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/cache.js`, `CACHE_FILENAME`) and renders them through `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/format-summary.js`'s `CATEGORIES` table (line 50).
- `#3973` provides `runLiveness(runDir, { now, probes }) -> { verdict: 'live' | 'dead' | 'unknown', evidence }` and the `owner` block in `run-state.json`.
- Tests: `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/archive-merged.test.js` (classifier fixtures), `tests/hooks-session-start.test.js` (banner), `tests/reconcile.test.js`.

## Deliverables

- [ ] A pure disposition function, `plugin/bin/lib/run-liveness/disposition.js` (next to the verdict module), taking run shape, liveness verdict, PR state, branch and worktree facts, and staged inventory, and returning `{ action: 'close' | 'leave' | 'orphan', reason, evidence, dropFindings }` and exporting the set of reasons that return `close` as `CLOSE_REASONS`. The ordered rules below are its contract, evaluated first match wins with a default of `leave`.
- [ ] A facts gatherer next to it (`plugin/bin/lib/run-liveness/facts.js`, injectable git and `gh` runners) that produces the inputs the function needs and maps any failed probe to the "cannot determine" value (never to a value that closes): `pr` is `merged | closed-unmerged | open | none | unknown`; `branch` is `{ localExists, remoteExists, uniqueCommits }` where `uniqueCommits` is a count against the integration branch's merge-base or `null` when it cannot be computed; `worktree` is `{ exists, dirty }` with `dirty` `null` when `git status` fails. `pr: 'unknown'` (a `gh`-absent environment, an API error, or the SessionStart fast path) and any `null` fact yield `leave` for every new row.
- [ ] The `live` skip: no archive path, existing ones included, acts on a run whose verdict is `live`. The skip is one guard at the top of the per-run loop in `archiveMerged`, which computes the verdict once per run and hands it to `classifyRunDir` as `ctx.liveness` (the classifier stays pure); a run directory with no `run-state.json` yields `unknown`. The existing merged, `orphaned-mint`, and `adhoc-superseded` paths gain only this skip and keep acting on `unknown`, each having its own evidence (a merged PR, a mint that never wrote `config.yml`, a worktree gone for 30 days). The existing `abandoned-interrupted` path also gains the skip; its own 24 hour recency test stays, and it keeps acting on `unknown`, until #3979 replaces it with the verdict.
- [ ] Reconcile evaluates the disposition for every non-clean run in REPORT-ONLY mode, behind one module constant `RUN_AUTO_CLOSE_REPORT_ONLY = true` in `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js` read at exactly one call site: it writes `would close {run} ({reason}, evidence ...)` lines to its summary and to `reconcile-cache.json` (`wouldClose`), lists the `orphan` runs in the same cache (`orphaned`, each with its PR number and reason) and in the archive check's `--json` output, reports a count of `unknown` runs in the summary (never in the banner), and closes nothing. Each pass records `reportOnlyPassAt` in `reconcile-cache.json`, the marker #3978 reads so that auto-close never acts on a checkout that has not first had a report-only pass. The summary renders wherever reconcile's summary already renders; a false positive is reported through `/claude-tweaks:feedback`.
- [ ] Banner: `collectStaleRuns` lists only runs that are `dead` and orphaned, newest run id first, keeps the 3-row cap, and adds an overflow line in the style of `CONSOLE_OVERFLOW_LINE`: `- … and {N} more orphaned run(s) (newest {MAX_REPORTED} shown): node "{root}/bin/hooks.js" reconcile --dry-run --json --checks archive`. The banner stays network-free: it reads the `orphaned` list from `reconcile-cache.json`, re-checks each entry's verdict offline with `runLiveness`, drops an entry that is no longer `dead`, and lists nothing for a run absent from the cache (nothing is listed before the first reconcile pass). Each row names its reason and a resume command, using the existing integrity-derived line text where it applies (the shipped-unclosed and consolidated-pass lines are kept as the text of rows that pass the filter). The "only the owning session should close a run" instruction text in `session-start.js` is removed.
- [ ] `session-end.js` closes and archives its own ad hoc run directly instead of marking it `interrupted`, keeping `events.jsonl` in the archive for `/claude-tweaks:feedback`. Order: append the `session-end` event first, then `closeRunState` (recording `closedBy: 'session-end'`) and `archiveRunDir`, with no write to the run directory afterwards (a late write would recreate the archived directory). It applies only when the `reason` on the SessionEnd input is one after which the session cannot continue (not `clear`, not `resume`) and when `staged/` is empty or holds only review findings; otherwise today's `interrupted` stamp is kept.
- [ ] `docs/reconcile-checks.md` documents the disposition table and the report-only switch; the switch is a release step, not a policy key.
- [ ] Review this repository's report-only output by hand before the enabling record; record the result in the PR body. Pass criterion: every `would close` line on a formal run names a run the maintainer agrees is abandoned; any disagreement blocks the enabling record until the disposition is fixed. The 27 stale formal runs measured on 2026-10-22 (20 open PRs, 6 closed-unmerged, 1 merged) are the review set; the 20 open-PR runs are `orphan` by design and the banner stays loud for them until their PR merges or closes or a human runs the abandon command.

The disposition rules, in order, first match wins, default `leave` ("staged ok" means `staged/` and every `spec-*/staged/` is empty or holds only review findings; "other staged" means any other kind):

| # | Run shape | Conditions | Disposition |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | any | verdict `live` | `leave`; never touched by any archive path |
| 2 | any | verdict `unknown` | `leave` for the new rows; existing paths keep acting on `unknown` |
| 3 | `-adhoc-standalone` | verdict `dead`, staged ok | `close` (no 30-day wait); `events.jsonl` moves with it |
| 4 | `-adhoc-standalone` | verdict `dead`, other staged | `orphan`, reason `staged items need an outcome` |
| 5 | other standalone (`-tidy-`, `-sweep-`, `-release-standalone`) | verdict `dead`, `staged/` empty | `close` |
| 6 | other standalone | verdict `dead`, `staged/` not empty | `leave` (the existing staged-proposals banner and #3898 own it) |
| 7 | formal | PR merged | `leave` here; the existing merged path acts, unchanged |
| 8 | formal | verdict `dead`, PR closed unmerged, staged ok | `close`, reason `pr-closed-unmerged`, `dropFindings` set |
| 9 | formal | verdict `dead`, PR closed unmerged, other staged | `orphan`, reason `staged items need an outcome` |
| 10 | formal | verdict `dead`, PR open (draft or ready) | `orphan`, reason `draft PR #N, session gone` or `PR #N open, session gone`; never closed |
| 11 | formal | verdict `dead`, no PR, (`uniqueCommits` greater than 0 or worktree dirty) | `orphan`, reason `unpushed commits on {branch}` or `uncommitted changes in {worktree}` |
| 12 | formal | verdict `dead`, no PR, (branch absent locally and on origin, or `uniqueCommits` 0), (worktree absent or clean), no owner-attributed event for 24 hours, staged ok | `close`, reason `nothing-to-resume`, `dropFindings` set |
| 13 | formal | verdict `dead`, no PR, otherwise as row 12 but other staged | `orphan`, reason `staged items need an outcome` |
| 14 | any | anything else (including any `unknown` fact: `pr: 'unknown'`, `uniqueCommits: null`, `dirty: null`) | `leave` |

Row 12's 24 hour floor is the existing `abandoned-interrupted` window (`STALE_INTERRUPTED_TTL_MS`) reused so a just-started or just-paused run is never closable sooner than today; the design table does not state it, and it only narrows what can close.

Staged items: for rows 8 and 12, review findings (the `review-unconfirmed-`, `review-contested-`, `review-debate-` kinds) would be dropped with reason `run-abandoned`, which report-only mode lists in `dropFindings` but does not do. Any other staged kind (reflect, queue write, skill update, `shadow-dup-*`) makes a run not closable and orphaned, as rows 4, 9 and 13 say. `run-abandoned` is introduced here as report vocabulary and registered in `_shared/auto-decision-log.md` by #3978, where the drop becomes real.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A fixture run whose owner PID is alive with a matching start time (a live-PID fixture) is never listed by the banner, never reported as `would close`, and is skipped by the merged, `orphaned-mint`, `adhoc-superseded`, and `abandoned-interrupted` paths; one test per path. The first three still act on an `unknown` fixture.
2. Each numbered rule of the disposition table has a test asserting its `action` and `reason`, including the default row; a run with verdict `unknown` yields `leave` for every new row, and `pr: 'unknown'`, `uniqueCommits: null`, and `dirty: null` each yield `leave` even when every other fact says close (a `gh`-absent fixture does not close a run whose PR was never seen).
3. Fail-open variants of the disposition function (treating verdict `unknown` as `dead`, and treating `pr: 'unknown'` as `none`) are present as injected faults and the corresponding tests fail against each.
   a. A falsely `interrupted` run (status `interrupted`, owner PID alive with a matching start time, as #3845 produces) is `live`: not listed, not `would close`, and left by the `abandoned-interrupted` path.
   b. The report-only constant is read at one call site (a source-scan test finds exactly one); with the constant set, the act path is unreachable (a test calling it with the constant true observes no write).
4. A reconcile run over a fixture containing a dead ad hoc run, a dead closed-unmerged-PR run, and a dead no-PR run with nothing to resume writes three `would close` lines to the summary and to `reconcile-cache.json`, and leaves every `run-state.json`, `staged/`, and directory byte-identical (a test snapshots the tree before and after).
5. A dead formal run with an open draft PR, and one with unique commits and no PR, yield `orphan`, appear in the banner, and are not in the `would close` lines.
6. A dead run holding a non-review staged item (for example `reflect-1.md`) yields `orphan` with reason `staged items need an outcome`; a dead closed-unmerged-PR run holding only `review-unconfirmed-*` items yields a `would close` line that also lists the findings it would drop with reason `run-abandoned`, and drops none.
7. With five dead orphaned runs in `reconcile-cache.json` the banner prints the newest three rows and one overflow line naming the remaining count (2) and the listing command; with three or fewer it prints no overflow line. With only `live`, `unknown`, or would-close runs, or with no cache, the banner prints nothing about runs. A cached orphan whose verdict is now `live` is dropped.
8. Each banner row names its reason (for example `draft PR #N, session gone`, `unpushed commits on {branch}`, `staged items need an outcome`) and a resume command; the text "only the session owning a run should close it" no longer appears in `session-start.js` (a grep test pins this).
9. `session-end.js`, given a session whose own run is ad hoc and a terminal SessionEnd reason, closes the run (status `clean`, `closedBy: 'session-end'`) and archives the directory including `events.jsonl`, with the `session-end` event appended before the archive and no write afterwards (the archived directory is not recreated); given a non-terminal reason (`clear`, `resume`), or an ad hoc run holding a non-review staged item, it stamps `interrupted` exactly as before; given a formal run it still stamps `interrupted` exactly as before; given a `fallback` attribution it touches nothing.
   a. The set of terminal reasons is taken from the SessionEnd `reason` values the harness actually emits (see the Gotchas probe), and the test enumerates each.
10. `docs/reconcile-checks.md` states that the new rows are report-only in this release and that the switch is deleted by the record that enables closing.

## Release Note

Added a dry-run report of runs that could be closed automatically, trimmed the unfinished-runs banner to runs that really need attention, and made sessions archive their own scratch run when they end.

## Technical Approach

The disposition function is pure (no I/O): reconcile gathers the facts (PR state from the existing merged-proof path, branch and worktree facts, staged inventory, the verdict from `runLiveness`) and passes them in, so the table is tested without a filesystem. Report-only is one module constant read at the single call site that would act, so the enabling record is a one-line flip plus deleting the constant.

The banner reuses the same disposition: it lists exactly the runs whose action is `orphan` and whose verdict is `dead`. A `would close` run is not listed in the banner (it is reconcile's to report) and is not closed in this release.

### Data / API Surface

`disposition({ shape, verdict, pr, branch, worktree, staged })` returns `{ action, reason, evidence, dropFindings: string[] }`, where `shape` is one of `adhoc`, `standalone`, `formal`; `pr` is `merged | closed-unmerged | open | none`; `dropFindings` lists staged files that would be dropped with reason `run-abandoned`. Reconcile's summary gains a `would-close` category (`format-summary.js`'s `CATEGORIES`) and `reconcile-cache.json` gains a `wouldClose` list of `{ runDir, reason, evidence }`.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/run-liveness/disposition.js` — new, the pure disposition function
- `plugin/bin/lib/run-liveness/index.js` — `runLiveness`, consumed (created by #3973)
- `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js` — `live` skip in `classifyRunDir`'s callers and the report-only evaluation
- `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/format-summary.js` — `would-close` summary category
- `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/cache.js` — `wouldClose` persisted in `reconcile-cache.json`
- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/session-residue.js` — `collectStaleRuns` filter, overflow line
- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/session-start.js` — banner render, removal of the owning-session warning text
- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/session-end.js` — close-and-archive of the session's own ad hoc run
- `docs/reconcile-checks.md` — disposition table and report-only switch

## Gotchas

- ASSUMPTION — verify at build: the resume command each banner row prints actually re-enters the run. Existing re-entry text in `collectStaleRuns` covers the shipped-unclosed and consolidated-pass cases; for `draft PR, session gone` and `unpushed commits` confirm what `/claude-tweaks:flow` adoption (`flow/preflight.js`'s `computeAdoption`) accepts before wording the command.
- ASSUMPTION — verify at build: the SessionEnd `reason` values the harness emits (for example `clear`, `resume`, and the exit reasons) and which of them leave the session running; probe it from a real hook invocation and record the raw values in the PR body before fixing the terminal set. Until verified, treat any reason other than a clearly terminal one as non-terminal.
- Reconcile must never act on `unknown`, and a probe error is `unknown`, never `dead`; do not add a shortcut that treats a missing `owner` block as dead (the legacy 72 hour route in `runLiveness` is the only legacy path to `dead`).
- The SessionEnd ad hoc close is safe only because the run is the ending session's own and ad hoc runs never resume (a resumed session mints a fresh one). Keep the `fallback`-attribution guard that `session-end.js` already has: a guessed run is never closed.
- Nested `claude -p` sessions (#3845) can fire SessionEnd against the parent's run. The ad hoc direct close must be gated on the same own-run attribution as the existing stamp, never on `ctx.runDir`.
- Report-only means no write of any kind to a run directory by the new rows: no `closedBy`, no `decisions.md` line, no archive move. The only writes are the summary and `reconcile-cache.json`.
- `reconcile` runs on a fast path at SessionStart (`FAST_CHECKS`) and a background path; the disposition needs PR state, which may require `gh`. Respect the existing gh-absent posture (`_shared/github-write-transport.md`'s MCP path and the accepted MCP gap documented in `docs/reconcile-checks.md`): without PR state a formal run is `leave`, not `close`.
- The banner currently skips ad hoc runs (`isAdHocRunDir`) so they cannot crowd out a real interrupted run; keep that skip for ad hoc and listing only `orphan` rows keeps the cap meaningful.
- File overlap with open records: `archive-merged.js` with #3975 (same file, sequential), #3945, #3740, and #3721; `session-residue.js` with #3950; `session-end.js` with #3845. Related: #2724 (the structurally-stuck tracker stays) and #3898 (release runs close at their own end there).
- Skill edges, if any, go in `docs/skill-graph.md` only; new reconcile checks follow `docs/reconcile-checks.md`'s "Adding a new check" registration list, including the `reconcile-threw` fallback duplicate in `hooks.js`.

**Related:** #3877

## Current State

After #3877, `/tidy`'s `## Arm ready PR` action (`plugin/skills/tidy/actions-github-issues.md`) holds a record-linked PR whose acceptance labeling never landed. That covers three cases: the run's `verify.json` `acceptance-labeling` row is not `pass`/`skip`, no `demo:pending` is set on its `Fixes` records, and no trusted brief/try-it run comment exists. In those cases the action logs a `SKIP` to `decisions.md` instead of arming.

`_shared/github-pr-scan.md`'s `repo-wide` item 9 still classifies that same PR as a granted `[pr-unarmed]` candidate on every sweep. So `tidy/step-6-auto.md` re-stages the same record-linked "Arm ready PR" row each run, and a human approves an arm that only holds again. `step-6-auto.md`'s own header treats a recurring staged item as a missing routing rule.

## Deliverables

- Item 9 (or tidy's Step 6 routing) applies the same acceptance-labeling landed check as the arm action. It reuses `dispatch/close-out.md` step 3's live-state precheck: `demo:pending` on every `Fixes` record, or a trusted brief/try-it run comment. Where a local run dir resolves, it also reads that run's `verify.json` `acceptance-labeling` row.
- A not-landed record-linked PR routes to **Yours**, carrying the paste-ready recommendation the arm action already names: `/claude-tweaks:dispatch close-out #{record}`, or the no-run-dir alternative. It does not appear as an Arm ready PR row.
- The arm action's own guard stays as the execution-time backstop.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A record-linked unarmed PR whose labeling has not landed surfaces under Yours with `/claude-tweaks:dispatch close-out #{record}` (or the no-run-dir alternative), not as an Arm ready PR row.
2. A record-linked PR whose labeling has landed still stages as an Arm ready PR row.
3. Housekeeping-marker PRs are unaffected.
4. `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

`/tidy` no longer keeps offering to arm a PR it will only hold for missing acceptance labeling.

## Technical Approach

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/_shared/github-pr-scan.md` — item 9 classifies a not-landed record-linked PR away from the Arm candidate set
- `plugin/skills/tidy/step-6-auto.md` — routes the not-landed record-linked flavor to Yours
- `plugin/skills/tidy/actions-github-issues.md` — arm guard stays as backstop; cross-reference the scan-time routing

groups.body:
Surface: infra

Origin: reflect full from #3783
**Related:** #205, #3783, #3740, #3508, #3706, #3721, #3905, #3936, #3946, #3963, #3973, #3974, #3975, #3976, #3977, #3979, #3982

## Current State

`plugin/skills/wrap-up/verification-brief-parent-gate.md` treats `$CLOSING_SUB_ISSUES` (the sub-issues a run is closing, which the parent gate counts as `CLOSED` while they are still open) as a prose contract. A table (around line 195) tells each sub-issue-side caller what to pass:

| Caller | Set it passes |
|---|---|
| wrap-up Phase 4 execution | the one sub-issue this run is closing |
| wrap-up auto-merge short-circuit | the one sub-issue this run is closing |
| dispatch group auto-merge gate (`settle-and-merge.md`) | every member of the group (the merge carries one `Fixes #{issue}` per record) |
| dispatch close-out step 3 (`close-out.md:77`) | the PR's `Fixes` record numbers |

Ruling #205 kept this as prose while three callers existed and set "a fourth sub-issue-side caller" as the revisit condition. #3783 (PR #3869) added the fourth (close-out step 3), and the file now defers the decision to this record. An omitted set defaults to `{the sub-issue in hand}`, so the silent-no-op mode is closed, but nothing checks a wrong non-empty set: a caller that passes the wrong records labels the wrong parent's gate.

Every row is a different description of one fact: the records the merge closes. Under `pr-first` that is the PR's `Fixes` lines, which GitHub reports as the PR's `closingIssuesReferences`. `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js` already reads that field (around line 320). Under `local-merge`/`current-branch` it is the wrap-up pack's `inputs.closingRecords` (`plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/pack.js`'s `closingRecords`), the same set the carrier commit's `Fixes` lines are composed from.

## Deliverables

- [ ] Ruling recorded in `verification-brief-parent-gate.md`: `$CLOSING_SUB_ISSUES` is **derived, not passed**. A shared helper computes it from the merge's own closing references, and the per-caller table becomes a description of that derivation.
- [ ] A `plugin/bin/` CLI (e.g. `closing-set.js`) returns the set as JSON: `--pr {n}` reads the PR's `closingIssuesReferences` (reusing `archive-merged.js`'s fetch shape); `--run {dir}` reads `wrap-up-pack.json`'s `inputs.closingRecords` for a run with no PR. An unreadable source exits non-zero with a reason and never prints `[]` as if nothing closes.
- [ ] All four callers call it instead of composing the set by hand: wrap-up Phase 4 execution (`execution-and-verification.md`), the auto-merge short-circuit (`auto-merge-short-circuit.md`), dispatch's group gate (`settle-and-merge.md`), and dispatch close-out step 3 (`close-out.md`)
- [ ] On a helper failure, keep today's default of `{the sub-issue in hand}`, and log the failure so the degraded set is visible
- [ ] A gh-absent (MCP transport) path, per `.claude/skills/mcp-agent-fetch-node-compute`: the agent fetches the PR's closing references through MCP and the helper reads them from a JSON file

## Acceptance Criteria

- Unit tests: a PR whose body closes `#1` and `#2` yields `[1, 2]`; a `--run` dir whose pack lists `[7]` yields `[7]`; a failed PR read and a missing pack each exit non-zero with a reason and print no set
- A conformance test asserts each of the four caller files invokes the helper and none composes `$CLOSING_SUB_ISSUES` by hand
- `verification-brief-parent-gate.md` carries the new ruling, keeps the `{the sub-issue in hand}` default as the failure fallback, and no longer defers to this record
- `npm test` passes

## Release Note

Parent acceptance gates compute which sub-issues a merge closes the same way at every merge site.

## Technical Approach

The original question was a helper versus prose with a new revisit condition. The trade-off it named, a helper "adds a code path every caller threads through" while "prose leaves a wrong non-empty set uncaught", only favors prose if the helper merely takes what the caller hands it. A helper that **derives** the set from the merge's own closing references removes the wrong-value risk entirely: the set equals what GitHub (or the carrier commit) will close, which is the definition the table was approximating. That is what makes the threading cost worth paying, and it also covers a fifth caller by construction instead of by a table row it might misread.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/closing-set.js` — new CLI
- `plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/closing-set.js` (or a sibling module) — derivation with an injectable runner
- `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js` — existing `closingIssuesReferences` read to reuse or extract
- `plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/pack.js` — `closingRecords` (local-merge source)
- `plugin/skills/wrap-up/verification-brief-parent-gate.md` — ruling and table
- `plugin/skills/wrap-up/execution-and-verification.md` — Acceptance labeling bullet
- `plugin/skills/wrap-up/auto-merge-short-circuit.md` — its `$CLOSING_SUB_ISSUES` line (around line 110)
- `plugin/skills/dispatch/settle-and-merge.md` — group gate
- `plugin/skills/dispatch/close-out.md` — step 3
- `docs/plugin-structure.md` — list the new CLI

## Gotchas

- The group gate labels **before** the merge lands, so `closingIssuesReferences` must be read from the open PR's body, not from a merged-PR event; confirm it is populated on an open draft PR whose body carries `Fixes #N` lines.
- `closingIssuesReferences` only lists same-repo issues linked by a closing keyword. A record the PR fixes without the keyword is not in the set, so that case keeps today's behavior: the gate sees it as still open.
- If extracting the shared read from `archive-merged.js`, follow `.claude/skills/shared-contract-extraction`'s migration discipline so reconcile's behavior is unchanged.

## Original request

Decide #205 revisit — shared helper for CLOSING_SUB_ISSUES now that four callers pass it

Origin: reflect full from #3783

Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State

`plugin/skills/wrap-up/verification-brief-parent-gate.md` keeps `$CLOSING_SUB_ISSUES` (the sub-issues a run is closing, read by the Self-inclusion rule) as a prose contract: each sub-issue-side caller reads the table there and passes its own set. Ruling #205 kept it prose while three callers existed and said to revisit it as a real code change once a fourth caller was added.

#3783 (PR #3869) added that fourth caller: `dispatch/close-out.md` step 3 now runs `_shared/pr-first-merge.md` Step 1 with `CLOSING_SUB_ISSUES` = the PR's `Fixes` records when a parked PR's labeling never landed. The parent-gate file now records that the condition is met and defers the decision to this record.

Nothing checks the value a caller passes: a wrong non-empty set labels the wrong records, which the default-to-the-sub-issue-in-hand rule does not catch.

## Deliverables

- A decision, recorded in `verification-brief-parent-gate.md`, on whether the closing set moves into a shared helper (for example a function that derives it from a PR's `Fixes` lines or a dispatch group) or stays a prose table.
- If a helper: every sub-issue-side caller (wrap-up Phase 4 execution, the auto-merge short-circuit, dispatch's group gate, dispatch close-out step 3) calls it, and a test pins each caller's use.
- If prose: the ruling states the new revisit condition.

## Open Question

Should `$CLOSING_SUB_ISSUES` become a shared helper now that four callers pass it, or stay a prose table with a new revisit condition? A helper adds a code path every caller threads through; prose leaves a wrong non-empty set uncaught.

## Release Note

Parent acceptance gates compute which sub-issues a merge closes the same way at every merge site.

## Technical Approach

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/wrap-up/verification-brief-parent-gate.md` — record the #205 revisit decision
- `plugin/skills/dispatch/close-out.md` — fourth caller passing CLOSING_SUB_ISSUES

Surface: infra

Origin: reflect hindsight from #3809
**Related:** #3973, #3736, #3744, #3822, #3876, #3900, #3915, #3974, #3975, #3978, #3979, #3983, #3989

## Current State

`plugin/skills/flow/worktree-merge.md` step 5's **Resolve now** bullet (line 127) carries a multi-run chase. A conflict resolution during a multi-run `local-merge` reconciliation ends in a `git commit`, and E1 (`runInner`'s tail loop in `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/pre-tool-use.js`) checks every commit against `ctx.runDir`, the newest non-terminal run in the project regardless of owner (`docs/hooks.md`'s "Two resolutions, not one"). The main checkout (or, under `worktree-always`, the scratch worktree the resolution runs in) is not any run's assigned worktree, so E1 denies unless the caller's ownership classifies as `foreign`, and the reconciling session usually owns the sibling runs. The procedure therefore closes this branch's run, then each other reconciliation branch's run E1 names in turn, and re-protects each one when the resolution lands or is abandoned.

That bullet drew #3809's whole-branch review Important 1, part of fix round 1, and four `/review` findings (3c at `:126` reproduced, plus single-agent 3b `:126`, 3c `:139`, 3f `:138`). The prose is correct today but is the most fragile part of the procedure, and it exists only because E1 cannot tell that a commit is concluding a merge of a live run's branch. E1's own deny message already names that case as legitimate ("If this checkout is intentionally correct (e.g. finishing the branch), clear the assignment first").

## Deliverables

- [ ] Add a live-query exemption to E1, of the same shape as `isIntegrationBranchFastForwardPush` (#2542): a `commit` target is allowed when its checkout has a merge in progress (a `MERGE_HEAD` exists) **and** every commit `MERGE_HEAD` lists equals the current `HEAD` of a live run's worktree (`ctx.runState.worktree` or any entry in E1's existing `otherWorktrees` map). Log a new `wd-merge-finish` event (expected, actual, merged run dir) to `ctx.runDir` and allow.
- [ ] Every unprovable answer keeps today's E1 verdict (no exemption): no readable `MERGE_HEAD`, a `MERGE_HEAD` commit matching no live run's worktree `HEAD`, a run worktree whose `HEAD` cannot be read (removed worktree, git failure, timeout), or a target action other than `commit`
- [ ] Simplify `worktree-merge.md` step 5's Resolve-now bullet: drop the E1 chase (closing and re-protecting other reconciliation branches' runs) and keep the per-branch close-run ordering #3809 pinned (this branch's run closed first, re-protected after a step 4 failure)
- [ ] Document the exemption in `docs/hooks.md` beside E1's posture bullets

## Acceptance Criteria

- In `tests/hooks-pre-tool-use.test.js`, a `git commit` in a checkout whose `MERGE_HEAD` equals a live sibling run's worktree `HEAD` is allowed and logs `wd-merge-finish`, while `ctx.runDir` names a different (newer) run
- The same commit is still denied when `MERGE_HEAD` is absent, when it names a commit that is no live run's worktree `HEAD`, when one of several `MERGE_HEAD` lines matches no live run, and when the matching run's worktree `HEAD` cannot be read. Each is its own test case.
- A `git push` or non-commit action is unaffected by the exemption
- Each new allow test goes red when the exemption is reverted (`git checkout --` on `pre-tool-use.js` only)
- `worktree-merge.md`'s Resolve-now bullet no longer instructs closing or re-protecting other branches' runs, and the existing #3809 ordering pins still pass
- `npm test` passes

## Release Note

Resolving a merge conflict during a multi-run local-merge reconciliation no longer has to close other branches' runs first.

## Technical Approach

The decision between the three signals the original request listed:

- **A run-state marker set and cleared by the reconciliation** was rejected. It adds a lifecycle (set before the merge, cleared on land or abandon) that the chase itself shows is fragile, and a marker left behind by a crash is a standing allow for that run's commits in the wrong checkout.
- **Narrowing E1's owner-unfiltered newest-run resolution in the main checkout** was rejected. The reconciling session usually owns the runs it merges, so their ownership verdict is `'mine'` and E1 would still deny. Narrowing further would also loosen E1 for the wrong-checkout commit it exists to catch.
- **A `MERGE_HEAD`-keyed live query** was chosen. Git already records the fact E1 lacks: a merge commit in progress whose parent-to-be is a live run's branch tip is that branch being integrated, not that run's work landing in the wrong checkout. It needs no new state, cannot go stale (git removes `MERGE_HEAD` when the merge concludes or aborts), and covers the `worktree-always` path too, where the resolution commits inside a scratch worktree that no run is assigned to.

Implementation follows `.claude/skills/pre-tool-use-gate-exemptions`: read `MERGE_HEAD` via `git rev-parse --git-path MERGE_HEAD` in the target's toplevel (a linked worktree's git dir differs from the main checkout's), compare commit ids exactly, read each candidate worktree's `HEAD` with `git -C {worktree} rev-parse HEAD`, resolve paths through `canonicalRealpath`, and fail closed on every inconclusive read.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/pre-tool-use.js` — E1 tail loop in `runInner`: the `MERGE_HEAD` live-query exemption and `wd-merge-finish` event
- `plugin/skills/flow/worktree-merge.md` — step 5 Resolve-now bullet: drop the E1 chase
- `docs/hooks.md` — E1 posture bullets
- `tests/hooks-pre-tool-use.test.js` — allow and fail-closed cases
- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/context.js` — `appendEvent` (no change expected)

## Gotchas

- The exemption must sit after the `otherWorktrees` check and before the `foreign`-ownership branch. That way it never reclassifies a commit already allowed as `wd-ambiguous`, and a `foreign` caller keeps its existing allow + `systemMessage`.
- Under `worktree-always`, the fast-forward of the main checkout is `git merge --ff-only`, which is not a `commit` target, so only the scratch-worktree commit needs the exemption. Confirm with `gitTargetsFrom` before assuming otherwise.
- An octopus merge lists several commits in `MERGE_HEAD`; require every line to match, so a merge that also pulls in an unrelated branch keeps today's deny.
- The `worktree-merge.md` bullet is pinned by #3809's conformance tests; keep "this branch's run is closed first" and the step 4 re-protection wording intact.

## Original request

Let E1 allow a multi-run reconciliation's conflict-resolution commit without closing sibling runs

Origin: reflect hindsight from #3809

Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State

`plugin/skills/flow/worktree-merge.md` step 5's **Resolve now** bullet carries a multi-run chase: the conflict resolution ends in a commit in the main checkout, which the working-directory hook (E1, `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/pre-tool-use.js`) checks against the newest non-terminal run in the project regardless of owner (`plugin/bin/hooks.js` resolveRunDir, owner-unfiltered). So before the commit can land, the procedure closes this branch's run, then every other reconciliation branch's run E1 names in turn, and must re-protect each one when the resolution lands or is abandoned.

That one bullet drew #3809's whole-branch review Important 1, part of fix round 1, and four /review findings (3c at :126 reproduced, plus single-agent 3b :126, 3c :139, 3f :138). The prose workaround is correct now but is the most fragile part of the procedure, and it exists only because E1 cannot tell that a main-checkout commit belongs to a human-present reconciliation.

## Deliverables

Decide how E1 should treat a commit in the main checkout made while reconciling several runs' branches — so the reconciliation does not have to close sibling runs to get its resolution commit through — and implement that decision in the hook.

Then simplify `plugin/skills/flow/worktree-merge.md` step 5's Resolve-now bullet to drop the E1 chase, keeping the per-branch close-run ordering #3809 pinned.

## Open Question

Which signal should let E1 allow this commit without closing other runs: a run-state marker that the reconciliation sets (and clears) on each run it is merging, a reconciliation-scoped exemption keyed on MERGE_HEAD naming a branch whose run is in the reconciliation, or narrowing E1's owner-unfiltered newest-run resolution for the main checkout? Each changes the never-break-a-session posture in docs/hooks.md differently.

## Release Note

Resolving a merge conflict during a multi-run local-merge reconciliation no longer has to close other branches' runs first.

## Technical Approach

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/pre-tool-use.js` — E1 decision for a reconciliation commit in the main checkout
- `plugin/skills/flow/worktree-merge.md` — drop step 5's E1 chase

## Plan Review Clarifications

Decided by the user at plan review (2026-10-30), from the plan-review question comment on this record:

- Q1 (which runs a MERGE_HEAD line may match): Reading A — keep the live-only candidate set exactly as Deliverables 1-2 and the second Acceptance Criterion say (`ctx.runState.worktree` or an `otherWorktrees` entry; a `status: clean` run's `worktreeAtClose` never counts). Amend Deliverable 3: Resolve now no longer closes this branch's run before the resolution commit. The run stays live (it was never closed after a step-2 predicted conflict, and it was re-protected after a step-4 failure), so the exemption matches its worktree HEAD. Run step 3's close-run fence for that run only once the resolution lands (after `git commit --no-edit --cleanup=strip`, or after the `worktree-always` fast-forward). An abandoned resolution therefore has no run closed for it. Keep the step 3 fence order and the AC3 phrases in `tests/local-merge-close-run-ordering.test.js` passing. No test pins the "closed first" wording, so the Gotcha that says to keep it no longer applies.
- Q2 (run-less reconciliation branch): drop the E1 chase entirely (Deliverable 3). If E1 still denies the resolution commit of a branch that has no run, run `git merge --abort`, report the deny, and handle the branch as **Skip this branch**: merge the remaining branches first (each run is closed at step 3 as its branch merges), then return to this branch from step 1. If E1 still denies on the return, treat the resolution as abandoned and report the run E1 named. No other branch's run is closed or re-protected to get the commit through.

**Related:** #2799, #2713, #3813, #3902, #3925, #3965

## Current State

`plugin/skills/visualize/SKILL.md` treats `/review` as a soft-hook caller that passes `--source review`:

- the "Used by" diagram (around line 15) lists `/claude-tweaks:review (Lens 3i-diagram)`
- the `--source <caller>` Input bullet (line 49), marked producer-only, names `review` among the callers that set it
- the Step 3 placement table (line 90) defines a `review` row: "Ephemeral by default; ask before persisting near `docs/architecture.md`"
- the Component-Skill Contract (around line 134) names `/claude-tweaks:review` as an invoker

`plugin/skills/review/step3-doc-freshness-lens.md` (Lens 3i-diagram, around line 35) never invokes `/visualize`. It emits an informational finding, "Visual documentation gap: … no matching diagram found. Consider `/claude-tweaks:visualize {type} {topic}`", routed "Suggest to user in wrap-up", with no `--source`. The finding fires only when the persistent diagram location for the change (`docs/journeys/`, `docs/plans/`, or `docs/diagrams/`) has no matching file. `docs/skill-graph.md:635` records the divergence.

## Deliverables

- [ ] Make `/review`'s side canonical (the original record's option b): remove `review` from `visualize/SKILL.md`'s "Used by" diagram, the `--source` callers list, the Step 3 placement table, and the Component-Skill Contract's invoker list
- [ ] Leave `step3-doc-freshness-lens.md`'s recommendation as a plain direct invocation (`/claude-tweaks:visualize {type} {topic}`, no `--source`). If the "Used by" diagram should still mention review, describe it as recommending a direct invocation, not as a caller
- [ ] Update `docs/skill-graph.md`'s `/visualize` section `/review` row to state the settled relationship: review recommends a direct invocation; it is not a `--source` caller

## Acceptance Criteria

- `visualize/SKILL.md`'s placement table has no `review` row, and its `--source` callers list names only `journeys` and `specify`
- `visualize/SKILL.md` no longer names `/claude-tweaks:review` as an invoker in its Component-Skill Contract
- `step3-doc-freshness-lens.md`'s finding text is unchanged
- `docs/skill-graph.md`'s `/review` row no longer describes a divergence
- `npm test` passes, including any skill-graph or `/help` diagram conformance suites

## Release Note

No user-visible change.

## Technical Approach

The two options in the original record decide where a `/review` diagram suggestion lands, and the lens's own trigger settles it. Lens 3i-diagram fires only when a **persistent** diagram for the changed area is missing, so its finding is a documentation gap. An ephemeral-by-default placement (option a) would fill that gap with a scratch file and leave the gap open. A plain direct invocation already runs `/visualize`'s Step 3 persist-or-show-me question, offering "Save as a project doc" to `docs/diagrams/`, which is what a gap needs. `--source` is also documented as producer-only, set by a caller that invokes `/visualize` itself. `/review` only recommends a command for the user to run in wrap-up, so it was never a producer. Option b deletes a dead placement row and keeps the recommendation honest.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/visualize/SKILL.md` — Used-by diagram, `--source` callers, placement table, Component-Skill Contract
- `plugin/skills/review/step3-doc-freshness-lens.md` — read-only check that the recommendation stays a direct invocation
- `docs/skill-graph.md` — `/visualize` section, `/review` row (line 635)

## Gotchas

- CLAUDE.md's Cross-references rule: every skill relationship is stated once, in `docs/skill-graph.md`. Removing the "caller" framing from `visualize/SKILL.md` must not leave a restated edge behind there.
- `/help`'s workflow diagrams must list all skills; check whether any diagram draws a `/review → /visualize` arrow labelled as a soft hook, and relabel it if so.

groups.body:
Surface: infra

Origin: ledger resolve gate (wrap-up of #3664, ledger rows 3-4)
**Related:** #3664, #3646, #3792, #3942

## Current State

The ephemeral dev server a pipeline starts (`_shared/dev-url-detection.md`'s Ephemeral server start, items 3-4) is recorded as one line, `{pid} {port} {worktree-root} detached:{yes|no}`, in `ephemeral-server.txt`. POSIX launches under `setsid` and records `detached:yes`; Windows has no detach primitive and records `detached:no` (`dev-url-detection.md:130-131`). The recorded pid is the shell leader; the listening socket can belong to its child.

Every stop identifies the server only by that pid and port. `wrap-up/cleanup-procedures-execution.md` Section D (#3664) validates the record's shape and keeps it when the port is still held after the kill, but proves neither identity:

- **Kill side (step 2):** any positive-integer pid is signalled (`kill {pid}`, plus `kill -- -{pid}` under `detached:yes`; `taskkill /PID {pid} /T /F` on win32). A pid reused by an unrelated process after the server died gets killed, along with its tree on win32.
- **Port side (step 4):** a port still held after an "already stopped" pid is reported as the server's survivor, though the holder may be an unrelated process.

A "pid listens on port" probe does not settle it, because the listener is usually the leader's child, and after the leader dies a non-detached child is reparented, so a parent-chain walk breaks.

The same stop logic is restated as agent-read prose in other places: `review/step3-routing.md`'s fix-wave server coordination (around line 124), `_shared/dev-url-detection.md`'s standalone stop, `flow/multispec-review-console.md`'s shared teardown (line 176), and `flow/multispec-parallel-waves.md`'s per-member stop (line 54). Each guard is pinned by text, not by behavior.

## Deliverables

- [ ] **Identity rule:** a process is identified by `(pid, start time)`. When the server starts, capture two identities: the **leader** (the pid recorded today) and the **listener** (the process holding the port once the readiness poll in item 3 succeeds). Write both, with start times, to a sidecar `ephemeral-server.json` beside `ephemeral-server.txt`. The txt line keeps its format, since `detached:` is parsed as its last token.
- [ ] **Kill side:** signal a recorded process only when its current start time matches the recorded one; a mismatch or a missing pid is "already stopped". Under `detached:yes`, the group kill stays keyed on the verified leader.
- [ ] **Port side:** after the kill, a port holder is the server's survivor only when it matches the recorded listener identity, or (under `detached:yes`) its process group is the recorded leader's. Any other holder is reported as "port {port} held by unrelated pid {x}", and the record is deleted, since the recorded server is gone.
- [ ] **One executable helper:** add a `plugin/bin/` CLI (e.g. `dev-server.js` with `record` and `stop` verbs, using the injectable-runner seam in `.claude/skills/gh-api-module-pattern`'s CLI wrapper contract). Every prose site above calls it instead of restating the stop: the Ephemeral server start's item 4 (record), Section D, `step3-routing.md`, the standalone stop, and both `/flow` multi-spec teardown sites (stop).
- [ ] **Legacy records:** a run whose record has no sidecar (started before this change) keeps today's behavior, logged once as `identity unverified (legacy record)`. Give that branch a removal condition per this repo's deprecation rule.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Unit tests with a fake process table: a recorded pid whose start time differs is not signalled and reports already stopped; a matching one is signalled; a port held by the recorded listener (alive after a leader-only stop) is reported as the survivor and the record is kept; a port held by an unrelated process is reported as unrelated and the record is deleted; a `detached:yes` child in the leader's process group counts as the survivor
- Each of those tests goes red against a helper that skips the identity check
- A conformance test asserts that none of the stop sites restate `kill {pid}` / `taskkill /PID` / an `lsof … | xargs kill` stop inline and that each one calls the helper
- A live probe on macOS (and Linux in CI where available) starts a real `setsid` shell-leader server, records it, and stops it through the helper, with the leader and listener identities matching what `ps` reports
- `npm test` passes

## Release Note

Pipeline cleanup no longer signals a process that merely reused a dead dev server's pid, and no longer blames an unrelated process for a port it failed to free.

## Technical Approach

The two candidate rules in the original question were a pid-listens-on-port probe (it fails for the shell-leader/child shape, as the record notes) and some stronger identity. Start time is the standard way to tell a reused pid from the original. POSIX: `ps -o lstart= -p {pid}` or `ps -o etimes=`; win32: `Win32_Process.CreationDate` via PowerShell `Get-CimInstance`. A reused pid cannot share its predecessor's start time. Capturing the listener's own identity at start, instead of deriving it from the leader at stop, sidesteps the reparenting problem entirely.

Listener lookup at record time: POSIX `lsof -nP -iTCP:{port} -sTCP:LISTEN -t`, with `ss -ltnp` as a fallback where `lsof` is absent; win32 `Get-NetTCPConnection -LocalPort {port} -State Listen` → `OwningProcess`.

Fail direction: an identity the helper cannot read (no `ps`, a CIM failure) is unprovable, so it signals nothing and reports a cleanup failure, keeping the record. A leaked dev server is recoverable; a killed unrelated process is not.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/dev-server.js` — new CLI: `record` and `stop` verbs
- `plugin/bin/lib/dev-server/` — new module: identity capture, verify, stop (injectable runner)
- `plugin/skills/_shared/dev-url-detection.md` — Ephemeral server start item 4 (record via helper), standalone stop
- `plugin/skills/wrap-up/cleanup-procedures-execution.md` — Section D steps 2-4 call the helper
- `plugin/skills/review/step3-routing.md` — fix-wave server coordination
- `plugin/skills/flow/multispec-review-console.md` — shared teardown step 1
- `plugin/skills/flow/multispec-parallel-waves.md` — per-member server stop
- `tests/bin-lib/dev-server/` — unit tests with a fake process table
- `docs/plugin-structure.md` — list the new CLI and module

## Gotchas

- ASSUMPTION — verify at build: `ps -o lstart=` and `Get-CimInstance Win32_Process` return a start time stable enough to compare exactly (second resolution) on the CI runners; if `etimes` is used instead, compare with a small tolerance and test the boundary.
- ASSUMPTION — verify at build: once the readiness poll succeeds, the listener is already bound and visible to `lsof`/`ss`/`Get-NetTCPConnection` without elevated privileges on macOS, Linux CI, and win32 CI. The original record noted no probe had been run against a real `detached:no` / `detached:yes` leader — run one before relying on it.
- The `bin/` CLIs must not read `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` at runtime (unset in Bash); follow the existing CLIs' process-cwd anchoring.
- `multispec-parallel-waves.md`'s members may start servers without a run-dir sidecar path; check where each member writes its record before wiring the helper.

## Original request

wrap-up Section D never proves the recorded pid or port belongs to the server it recorded

Origin: ledger resolve gate (wrap-up of #3664, ledger rows 3-4)

Defer-reason: needs-human-decision

## Current State

wrap-up Section D (`plugin/skills/wrap-up/cleanup-procedures-execution.md`) identifies the dev server it stops only by the pid and port in `ephemeral-server.txt`. #3664 made it validate the record's shape (four fields, positive-integer pid and port, a `detached:` token) and keep the record when the port is still held after the kill, but nothing proves the recorded pid is still the server it was recorded for. Kill side: step 2 signals any positive-integer pid, so a pid reused by an unrelated process after the server died is signalled. Port side: step 4 reports a port still held after an "already stopped" pid as the survivor, though the holder may be an unrelated process. A pid-listens-on-port probe does not settle it: a `detached:no` or `detached:yes` record names the shell leader, and the listening socket belongs to its child. The stop logic is also agent-read prose in three places (Section D, review's fix-wave server coordination in `step3-routing.md`, and the standalone stop in `_shared/dev-url-detection.md`), so each guard is pinned by text, not by behavior. Refs #3664 (its review ledger rows 3-4).

## Deliverables

- [ ] Decide the identity rule: how the recorded server is told from an unrelated process on the recorded pid (kill side) and on the recorded port (port side), covering the shell-leader and child-socket record shapes on POSIX and win32.
- [ ] Apply the rule in every place that stops a recorded dev server, preferably through one executable stop helper the three prose sites call, so the rule is tested by behavior.
- [ ] Pin it with a test that fails against the current text.

## Open Question

Which identity check is sound for the shell-leader and child-socket shapes `ephemeral-server.txt` legitimately records, and is a single executable stop helper the right home for it? Insufficient evidence: no probe has been tried against a real `detached:no` / `detached:yes` leader.

## Release Note

Pipeline cleanup no longer signals a process that merely reused a dead dev server's pid, and no longer blames an unrelated process for a port it failed to free.

## Technical Approach

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/wrap-up/cleanup-procedures-execution.md` — modify
- `plugin/skills/review/step3-routing.md` — modify
- `plugin/skills/_shared/dev-url-detection.md` — modify

## Plan Review Clarifications

Decided by the user at plan review (2026-10-30), from the plan-review question comment on this record:

- Q1 (standalone stop): Reading A — outside a pipeline, the Ephemeral server start also calls `dev-server.js record`, which writes the same `ephemeral-server.txt` line and `ephemeral-server.json` sidecar into a per-server directory `dev-server-{port}/` under the session temp root (`_shared/session-tmp-root.md`'s `sessionTmpPath($CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, …)`, falling back to unscoped `os.tmpdir()` when there is no session id). The standalone stop calls `dev-server.js stop` on that directory. `record` and `stop` accept that directory under the anchored-or-outside rule: they refuse a path inside any checkout that is not anchored under the main checkout, and accept a path outside every checkout. They append no `decisions.md` entry on this path.
- Q2 (go-red criterion): Reading A — keep the criterion as written: all five fake-process-table tests must fail against a helper that skips the identity check. Each positive scenario (matching leader signalled, recorded listener survivor, `detached:yes` group-child survivor) also puts a reused-pid process with a different start time in the table, and asserts it is neither signalled nor reported as the survivor. The unrelated-holder test also asserts that nothing is signalled. The build proves each red by running the five tests against an identity-skipping mutant.

Origin: reflect hindsight from #4548

## Current State

On #4548, `/claude-tweaks:review` Step 3.7 dispatched eighteen read-only tiebreak agents, and two of them ran `git stash` by accident. Each put a backtick-quoted token (a code span such as `git stash`) inside a double-quoted `git grep` argument, and the shell executed it as a command substitution. The worktree was clean, so nothing was stashed. In a dirty worktree, the stash would have swept a sibling's edit into the shared, repo-wide stash stack.

Since this record was filed, the tiebreak template (`plugin/skills/review/step3-tiebreak.md:62-63`) no longer carries shell rules of its own. It inlines two lines verbatim from the composed review-dispatch bundle, via placeholders:

- the `READ-ONLY REVIEW:` line (`plugin/skills/_shared/subagent-dispatch-core.md:151`), which is about not running suites, builds or servers
- the `SHELL DISCIPLINE:` line (`subagent-dispatch-core.md:43`)

The same `SHELL DISCIPLINE:` placeholder sits in the lens, debate, refutation, and gap-sweep templates (`plugin/skills/review/step3-lens-dispatch.md:56`, `plugin/skills/review/step3-debate-and-refutation.md:38`, `:104`, `:138`) and in `/tidy`'s console backfill (`plugin/skills/tidy/console-backfill.md:113`). So that one line is the single copy every read-only reviewer prompt receives.

The line says one plain command per call, literal absolute paths, no shell-variable paths, no `cd … &&`, and no heredoc in a compound command, and it says to read files with the Read and Grep tools. It never warns that a backtick inside a double-quoted shell argument is executed. `tests/review-lens-shell-discipline-conformance.test.js` (`assertShellLine`, lines 44-55) pins the line's existing clauses one regex each, with a go-red case (lines 61-67).

## Deliverables

1. Add one clause to the `SHELL DISCIPLINE:` line in `plugin/skills/_shared/subagent-dispatch-core.md`. It should say: never put a backtick inside a double-quoted shell argument, because the shell runs it as a command; pass a search pattern containing a backtick in single quotes, or search with the Grep tool. Keep the line a single backtick-delimited prompt line, as the conformance test's `^`SHELL DISCIPLINE: [^`]+`$` shape requires. Spell the backtick out in words rather than writing a literal backtick inside the code span.
2. Extend `assertShellLine` in `tests/review-lens-shell-discipline-conformance.test.js` with one regex for the new clause, so a bundle that drops it goes red.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The `SHELL DISCIPLINE:` line in `subagent-dispatch-core.md` carries the backtick-in-double-quotes warning and still matches `^`SHELL DISCIPLINE: [^`]+`$`.
- The composed review-dispatch bundle (`compose` over `subagent-dispatch-core.md` + `run-dir-resolution.md`, as the test builds it) carries the clause.
- `assertShellLine` asserts the clause. Deleting the clause from `subagent-dispatch-core.md` turns `node --test tests/review-lens-shell-discipline-conformance.test.js` red, and restoring it turns it green.
- `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

Stop read-only review agents from running commands by accident when a search pattern contains a backtick.

## Technical Approach

A single-copy prose edit plus one test assertion. The tiebreak template and every other review dispatch inline the bundle's `SHELL DISCIPLINE:` line verbatim through placeholders, so editing that line reaches all of them. No template needs its own copy; adding one would create a second copy to drift. The warning belongs in the shell-discipline line rather than the `READ-ONLY REVIEW:` line, because it is a shell-quoting rule, not a what-may-run rule.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/_shared/subagent-dispatch-core.md` — add the backtick-in-double-quotes clause to the `SHELL DISCIPLINE:` line (line 43)
- `tests/review-lens-shell-discipline-conformance.test.js` — one new regex in `assertShellLine`

## Gotchas

- The original Deliverables named the tiebreak template and the `READ-ONLY REVIEW:` line's neighbours as two places to add the sentence. Since then the tiebreak template switched to verbatim placeholders (`step3-tiebreak.md:62-63`), so a second hand-written copy there would bypass the bundle and drift. One edit to the bundle line covers every review dispatch.
- The `SHELL DISCIPLINE:` line is itself an inline code span. A literal backtick inside it would end the span early and break the `^`SHELL DISCIPLINE: [^`]+`$` assertion. Describe the character in words ("a backtick").
- Implementer dispatches state the shell rule in their own prompts (`subagent-dispatch-core.md:41`, "an implementer or other dispatch states the rule above in its own prompt") and do not receive this line. They are outside this record's read-only-reviewer scope.
- #4243 (ready) carries the worktree shell constraint into `/build`'s dispatch prompts and also lists `subagent-dispatch-core.md` among its files. If it is in flight, rebase onto it before editing line 43. Neither record depends on the other's change.
- The prompt line must stay outside any byte-pinned Calibration/Output block. The test's `doesNotMatch` check on the Calibration region (around line 78) keeps that true.

## Original request

Surface: terminal

Origin: ledger resolve gate (record #3313, build item 14)
**Related:** #3313, #2987, #3002, #3933

## Current State

A project's `verify-scope.json` can declare `preExisting`: a glob/path allowlist of known-failing test files (#3129; e.g. a shallow clone's precondition tests). A run whose entire failing-file set is covered by it is adjudicated as passing (`plugin/bin/verify.js` around line 616). #3313 added a report-only new/fixed split (`newAndFixed` in `plugin/bin/lib/verify/pre-existing.js`): "fixed" lists the tracked test files an entry covers that did not fail. It is computed only inside the adjudication block, gated on `!rawPass && !adjudicatedPass` (`verify.js:632`), and only for a full-scope run with every check run.

A green (raw-pass) run never enters that block, so it never reports that its `preExisting` entries went unused. Because `verify-scope.json` is a committed project file, an entry that is no longer needed stays a standing waiver: if that file later breaks again for a real reason, its failure is excused without anyone seeing it.

## Deliverables

- [ ] On a raw-pass, full-scope run (every check ran) with a non-empty `preExisting` declaration, print one report line: none of the N declared `preExisting` entries was needed in this run, naming the entries
- [ ] Narrower scope modes (`affected` and the like) print nothing, since they did not run every suite and cannot claim a listed file passed (the same rule `newAndFixed` already applies)
- [ ] The line is informational: it never changes the exit code or the verify stamp, and never tells the reader to delete the entries. Entries are often environment-specific (a test that fails only in a shallow clone passes locally), so the line reads "not needed in this run", not "stale, remove"
- [ ] Add the same fact to the run's JSON/report output beside the existing `preExistingAdjudicated` field (for example `preExistingUnused: { declared, mode }`), so `/test` and the wrap-up pack can surface it
- [ ] Document the line in `plugin/skills/test/verification.md`'s `preExisting` paragraph

## Acceptance Criteria

- A raw-pass full-scope run with `preExisting: ["tests/a.test.js"]` prints the not-needed line naming `tests/a.test.js`, and its JSON carries `preExistingUnused`
- A raw-pass run in a narrower scope mode, a run with no `preExisting` key, and a failing run each print no such line
- The line does not alter the exit code or the stamp (asserted by comparing to the same run without the declaration)
- No `git ls-files` call is made on the raw-pass path (asserted with the injectable `execImpl`)
- `npm test` passes

## Release Note

`verify` now notes when a full green run didn't need any of the declared pre-existing-failure allowances.

## Technical Approach

The original question offered three postures: report on every pass, only under full scope, or only behind a flag. Full scope only, by default, is the one that is both sound and cheap:

- **Sound:** only a full-scope run with every check run exercised every suite, which is the same reason `newAndFixed` returns `fixed: null` for narrower modes.
- **Cheap:** the cost the original record worried about was `git ls-files` on every green run. On a raw pass no test failed, so every declared entry was unneeded by definition, and the line can name the declared entries directly with no tracked-file enumeration. The output cost is one line, only for projects that declare `preExisting`, which is meant to be temporary.
- **Not behind a flag:** a flag would leave the standing-waiver risk invisible, which is the gap this record exists to close.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/verify.js` — raw-pass branch: emit the line and the `preExistingUnused` field
- `plugin/bin/lib/verify/pre-existing.js` — optional small helper for the raw-pass report (no `trackedFiles` call)
- `plugin/skills/test/verification.md` — document the line beside the existing `preExisting` paragraph
- `tests/bin-lib/verify/` — new cases for the line, the narrower-mode silence, and the no-`ls-files` assertion

## Gotchas

- `verify.js`'s stdout is bounded by contract ("one table row per check plus at most one ≤100-line failing region", `verification.md:58`); the new line has to fit that contract's wording, so update the bound's description if it enumerates every line kind.
- Keep the report out of stamp-match logic: `verify.js:142` treats a `preExisting`-adjudicated stamp differently, and a raw pass that merely reports unused entries is still a plain raw pass.

## Original request

Decide whether a green verify run should flag stale preExisting allowlist entries

Origin: ledger resolve gate (record #3313, build item 14)

Defer-reason: needs-human-decision

## Current State

#3313 made `verify.js` report which allowlisted `preExisting` files passed ("N new, M fixed") — but only on a run that failed and was adjudicated. A green (raw-pass) run never adjudicates, so a fully stale allowlist, where every entry now passes, is never flagged for removal. Files: `plugin/bin/verify.js`, `plugin/bin/lib/verify/pre-existing.js`, `plugin/skills/test/verification.md`.

## Deliverables

- [ ] Decide whether a raw-pass run with a `preExisting` declaration should print the fixed list.
- [ ] If yes, implement it and pin the cost of `git ls-files` on every green run.

## Open Question

Should a green run pay for the stale-allowlist check on every pass, only under scope mode full, or only on request (a flag)? Printing it by default adds output to the most common run; a flag keeps a stale allowlist invisible unless someone asks.

## Release Note

No user-visible change until the question is answered.

Surface: infra

Origin: ledger resolve gate (wrap-up of #3475, whole-branch review Minor 3)
**Related:** #3419, #3475, #3370, #3973, #3977, #3978

## Current State

`docs/hooks.md:24` (**Every inform-tier line names its relay**, #3419) requires a SessionStart inform-tier line that carries a runnable command to also say `never run it yourself`, because `additionalContext` reaches the model, not the user, and an autonomous run may otherwise execute it. After #3475, the unfinished-runs banner (`plugin/bin/lib/hooks/session-start.js:170`) and the staged-proposals banner (`:195`) comply.

The unreviewed-console-residue banner (`session-start.js:208-215`, #3370) does not. It lists closed or archived runs whose unattended Review Console "left item(s) no human has reviewed", each with a runnable `console-residue.js --ack --run …` command, plus `consoleAckAllLine` (`plugin/bin/lib/hooks/session-residue.js:202`). Its trailer tells the model to "Read each item, then act on it (apply it, file it with /claude-tweaks:capture, or drop it) and mark the run reviewed with its own command above", which directs the model to run the ack itself.

The banner and the rule disagree, and nothing records which is intended.

## Deliverables

- [ ] Bring the console-residue banner under the #3419 rule: its trailer tells the model to relay each item with its command to the user and **never run the `--ack` / `--ack-all` commands itself**. The model acts on an item (apply, `/claude-tweaks:capture`, drop) or marks a run reviewed only when the user asks it to in this session.
- [ ] Reword "act on it … and mark the run reviewed" into a relay instruction. The banner's own heading ("no human has reviewed") stays the reason the decision belongs to the user.
- [ ] Pin the trailer's `never run it yourself` clause in `tests/hooks-session-start.test.js` beside the two existing banner pins, with a go-red control
- [ ] No carve-out is added to `docs/hooks.md`; the rule stays exceptionless for runnable lines

## Acceptance Criteria

- The console-residue banner's trailer contains the `never run it yourself` clause and no instruction to run `--ack` or act on items unprompted
- `tests/hooks-session-start.test.js` asserts the clause for the console-residue banner, and reverting the trailer turns that assertion red
- `docs/hooks.md`'s #3419 bullet is unchanged (no carve-out), and its list of compliant banners names the console-residue banner
- `npm test` passes

## Release Note

The session-start notice about unreviewed console items now asks you to review and acknowledge them, instead of telling Claude to do it on its own.

## Technical Approach

The decision the original record asked for, rule versus named carve-out, turns on what `--ack` asserts. The banner exists because an `unattended` run's Review Console resolved items with no human present (#3370), and `console-residue.js --ack` records that a human has now reviewed them. `--ack-all`'s own line already calls that "a human decision". If the model reads the items and acks them, the record says a human reviewed items no human saw, which is the very gap the banner exists to close. The model doing the acting is also what the unattended console already did. So the banner moves to the rule. A carve-out would make the residue banner's own purpose unreachable.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/session-start.js` — console-residue banner trailer (around lines 208-215)
- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/session-residue.js` — `consoleAckAllLine` wording (check it reads as a user-run command)
- `docs/hooks.md` — #3419 bullet's list of compliant banners
- `tests/hooks-session-start.test.js` — new pin beside the two existing banner pins

## Gotchas

- `consoleAckAllLine` is also used by `plugin/bin/hooks.js:1451`, which is not a SessionStart surface (the `check-session-residue` block the Review Console renders as an informational line). Leave that surface's wording alone unless its consumer also relays to a human. This change is about the SessionStart banner.
- The installed plugin build can lag `origin/main` (6.145.0's banners still lack the #3475 clause), so verify against the worktree's own `session-start.js`, not the installed copy.

## Original request

Reconcile the never-run rule with the console-residue SessionStart banner

Origin: ledger resolve gate (wrap-up of #3475, whole-branch review Minor 3)

Defer-reason: needs-human-decision

## Current State

docs/hooks.md (the 'Every inform-tier line names its relay' bullet) states that a SessionStart inform-tier line carrying a runnable command also says 'never run it yourself' (#3419). After #3475 the unfinished-runs and staged-proposals banners comply. The unreviewed-console-residue banner in plugin/bin/lib/hooks/session-start.js (the block that appends sessionResidue.consoleAckAllLine) does not: it carries runnable --ack commands and tells the model to read each item, act on it, and then 'mark the run reviewed with its own command above'. The rule and the banner disagree, and nothing records which one is intended.

## Deliverables

- [ ] Decide which side moves: add a never-run-it-yourself clause to the console-residue banner (the model relays and the user runs --ack), or record a named carve-out for it in docs/hooks.md because the banner deliberately has the model run --ack after reviewing
- [ ] Apply the decision in plugin/bin/lib/hooks/session-start.js and/or docs/hooks.md, and pin it in tests/hooks-session-start.test.js

## Open Question

Should the console-residue banner tell the model to relay its --ack commands and never run them itself (matching the #3419 rule), or is it a deliberate exception where the model acknowledges a run after reviewing its items, in which case the rule in docs/hooks.md needs a named carve-out?

## Release Note

No user-visible change.

Surface: infra

## Current State

`plugin/skills/_shared/github-pr-scan.md`'s repo-wide item 4 ("Merged/closed PRs with local remnants") runs two queries, `gh pr list --state merged --limit 50` and `gh pr list --state closed --limit 50`, and justifies running both with a parenthetical:

> GitHub's PR `state` is `OPEN`/`CLOSED`/`MERGED` — mutually exclusive — so `--state closed` never overlaps `--state merged`

That claim is wrong for the CLI filter. `gh pr list --state closed` returns merged PRs too: in the 2026-10-21 sweep, 47 of the 50 `--state closed` entries were merged (e.g. #3891). The scan still produces correct rows only because each `headRefName` from either result is cross-checked against local branches, so a PR appearing in both lists is harmless.

The wrong note has a second, unstated cost. Because merged PRs fill most of the closed query's 50-entry window, "closed without merging" PRs get only a few of the slots (3 of 50 in that sweep). A stale local branch from an abandoned PR is therefore easily pushed out of view.

## Deliverables

1. Correct item 4's parenthetical so it states the real CLI behavior: `--state closed` includes merged PRs.
2. Make item 4's handling of the overlap explicit: either dedupe the two result sets by PR number in the procedure text, or select closed-without-merge PRs directly so the second query no longer spends its window on merged PRs. The plan records which and why.
3. If item 4's window behavior changes, keep the closed-without-merge coverage at least as wide as today's.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Item 4's text no longer claims `--state closed` and `--state merged` are mutually exclusive, and states that the closed filter includes merged PRs.
- Item 4's procedure states how a PR present in both result sets is handled (deduped by number, or excluded by query shape).
- If the query shape changes, the closed-without-merge query's results contain only non-merged closed PRs (for example `gh pr list --state closed --json number,headRefName,mergedAt` filtered to `mergedAt == null`, or a search qualifier), verified by running the documented command against this repo and quoting its count in the PR.
- Any conformance test that pins item 4's prose (check `tests/` for `github-pr-scan` pins) passes after the edit, and `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

Tidy's GitHub scan now describes its merged and closed PR queries correctly and finds stale branches from abandoned PRs more reliably.

## Technical Approach

This is a prose edit to item 4 in `github-pr-scan.md`, which is read through `compose-context.js` bundles under the `pr-scan` step. If Deliverable 2 changes the query, the cleanest shape is a single `gh pr list --state closed --limit {n} --json number,headRefName,mergedAt` call split locally into merged and closed-unmerged sets. That replaces two partially-overlapping queries with one, and widens the closed-unmerged window instead of shrinking it. The alternative (keep both queries, add an explicit dedupe sentence) is a smaller edit but keeps the window cost. The plan picks one and says why the other lost.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/_shared/github-pr-scan.md` — repo-wide item 4 text and queries

## Gotchas

- `github-pr-scan.md` has transport-split rules: item 4 is PR-backed and degrades under the MCP transport. Keep the degrade note accurate if the query changes.
- Executable prose in `_shared/` may be byte-pinned by skill-prose conformance tests. Run the full suite after the edit.

## Original request

github-pr-scan item 4 wrongly treats the closed and merged PR lists as mutually exclusive

**Related:** none

Context: `gh pr list --state closed` also returns merged PRs (47 of 50 closed entries were merged in the 2026-10-21 sweep, e.g. #3891), so `_shared/github-pr-scan.md` repo-wide item 4's mutually-exclusive note is wrong; the scan works only because it dedupes by PR number.

Scope: correct the item 4 note and make the dedupe-by-number explicit (or filter the closed list by state).
